docs.text: 43 Chapter 2 Master Data Now that we’ve covered the PP/DS basics, it’s time to move on to master data. We’ll dive into the integration model and provide step-by-step instructions for setting up the master data objects. In this chapter, we’ll cover the master data objects in detail, beginning with the concept of integration models. Then, we’ll cover the individual master data objects such as materials, work centers, in-house production source of supply (e.g., production data structures [PDSs]), external procurement relationships (e.g., purchase info records, contracts, and scheduling agreements), classes, characteristics, setup matrices, quota arrangements, and time-dependent safety stocks.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For material masters and work centers (resources), there is no need to create an integra- tion model. But for certain master data objects, such as external procurement relation- ships, it’s still required to create integration modes with the self-system destination. We’ll also cover the concept of the integration model and all the master data objects required to execute the planning and scheduling in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA (embedded PP/DS). In addition, certain master data objects, such as characteristics-based setup matrices, quota arrangements, and time-dependent safety stock, are maintained in embedded PP/DS and don’t require integration with SAP S/4HANA. 2.1 Integration Models An integration model is an object used to transfer certain master data objects from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These integration models use the simplified core inter- face in the SAP S/4HANA system. The core interface is a real-time data exchange frame- work using the queued remote function call (qRFC) communication technology. Typically, there are source and target systems involved in transferring data from an ERP system to the PP/DS system. Because both ERP and PP/DS are part of the same system in SAP S/4HANA, the source and destinations are the same for the integration model. There are two steps involved in transferring the data via the integration model: 1.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Create the integration model. The process starts with creation of an integration model where the basic identifiers, such as the integration model name, the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization application name, and the logical systems, are defined. In addition, the selection and filter criteria for the master data objects are defined. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 44 2. Activate the integration model. The second step in transferring the master data to embedded PP/DS using the inte- gration model is the activation of the defined integration model. During the activa- tion, the data defined in the selection criteria for the integration model is packaged into the RFC queues and transferred to embedded PP/DS. We’ll walk through both steps in this section. 2.1.1 Create the Integration Model The creation of an integration model is executed using Transaction CFM1 via menu path, SAP Menu  Logistics  Central Functions  Supply Chain Planning Interface  Core Interface Advanced Planner and Optimizer  Integration Model  Create .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 2.1, the Model Name , Logical System , and APO Application uniquely identify the integration model. We’ll cover the logical system definition and the tech- nical details in Chapter 3. Note SAP S/4HANA can also be used as the ERP system with the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system. Therefore, the SAP S/4HANA integration model also supports the creation of an integration model for standalone SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi- zation systems. In addition, with SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, it’s also required to create an integration model for the transfer of data from the source SAP S/4HANA system to SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, where PP/DS is implemented.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll cover the details of SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA in Chapter 9. In this case, the integration model is created with the logical system defined for the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization or the SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA sys- tem, so you’ll see all the master data objects that can be integrated via the core interface in the integration model transaction. After SAP S/4HANA is selected as the logical sys- tem, only the master data objects that still require an integration model in embedded PP/DS are available for selection in the integration model transaction.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The material-dependent master data objects (e.g., contracts and purchase info records) and the material-independent master data objects (e.g., setup groups and classes) can also be transferred to embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA using the integration model. After the logical system is entered, and if it’s the one defined for the same SAP S/4HANA system, the system shows only the master data objects that are transferred through the integration model. Other master data objects are transferred to embedded PP/DS via generation reports or by setting the Advanced Planning checkbox in the master data objects (which we’ll discuss throughout this chapter). © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 53 2.2 Locations Note In embedded PP/DS, all the master data and transaction data items are assigned to a supply chain model and version. Versions can be created to simulate any planning- relevant parameters. 000 is the active model, and 000 version is the active version. The master and transaction data integrated into embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA is always assigned to the 000 version. For maintaining the PP/DS calendars, click on the Calendar tab and maintain the Pro- duction Calendar for scheduling the production activities and the Display Calendar (PPDS) for controlling the display of the periodic views in PP/DS planning tools such as the production planning table.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tip For creating PP/DS planning calendars, use Transaction /SAPAPO/CALENDAR. The handling resources in the location master are used by the goods receipt (GR) and goods issue (GI) processing operations. To support GR/GI processing times assigned in the product masters, the handling resources must be assigned in the location master. To maintain the resources, click on the Resources tab, and maintain the handling resources as shown in Figure 2.10. Resource Inbound is used in scheduling the GR activ- ities when GR processing is assigned in the material master, and Resource Outbound is used in scheduling GI activities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 54 The business partner master data is created in SAP S/4HANA, and depending on the role of the business partner, the role-specific data is added in SAP S/4HANA. Depending on whether the business partner is a vendor or customer, the same entity acts as a ven- dor and customer. In embedded PP/DS, the location mater data is used in transaction data objects. For example, the plant location data is used in in-house manufacturing orders such as planned orders and production orders, and the vendor location master data and customer location master data are used in the purchasing documents and sales documents, respectively.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The context for the transaction data is enhanced with the location master data details in embedded PP/DS. 2.3 Product Master In this section, we’ll cover the details of the product master in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA and how the material master maintained in the SAP S/4HANA system is transferred to embedded PP/DS. In the SAP S/4HANA system, the material master holds the informa- tion about the materials that a company manufactures, procures, and stores in its premises. Depending on the usage of the material in the company, different material types are defined.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Based on the type of material, such as raw material, semifinished material, or finished product, the relevant information is stored in the material master data. 2.3.1 Activation of Advanced Planning for Materials In the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the material master created in the ERP system must be transferred to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system via the core interface. In addition, the integration model is required to transfer the material master to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimiza- tion system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Change pointers are also implemented to send the material master changes to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system when a change is made in the ERP system. The material master data in SAP Advanced Planning and Opti- mization is called the product master, and any product master data from the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is directly maintained in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system. Due to the presence of the core interface layer between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and ERP sys- tems, there are challenges in monitoring the queues for any errors and correcting them to ensure the data consistency between the ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Opti- mization systems.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, there is no need to create an integration model for the material master. As PP/DS is part of the SAP S/4HANA core, the material master created in SAP S/4HANA is available for PP/DS by activating the material for advanced planning. There is a new view in the SAP S/4HANA material master where the PP/DS-specific master © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 55 2.3 Product Master data can be maintained. Therefore, the maintenance of the material master is only pos- sible from the ERP side transaction within the SAP S/4HANA system, and the PP/DS product master is a display-only view. As shown in Figure 2.11, from the material master Transaction MM01 (Create Material) or Transaction MM02 (Change Material), navigate to the Advanced Planning tab, and check the Advanced Planning checkbox on the material master. This checkbox immedi- ately makes the material master available for PP/DS planning upon saving the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, activating Advanced Planning will populate the mandatory fields, such as the PP Plng Procedure in the material master. Once you activate the Advanced Planning checkbox and press (Enter) , you’ll see that the Not relevant for planning field is changed to Active for planning . You can activate a material for advanced planning, but it can be deactivated if planning of the material is no longer required in PP/DS. In this case, the material is still integrated to embedded PP/DS, but no planning or changes are possible in PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 2.11 Activation of Advanced Planning in SAP S/4HANA Material Master Any additional PP/DS master data that is relevant for specific planning scenarios within PP/DS can be maintained in this Advanced Planning tab. As shown in Figure 2.12, the PP/DS data is stored in SAP S/4HANA material master table MARC . The PP/DS data- base tables (e.g., table /SAPAPAO/MATLOC ) are just a view of the data stored in table MARC , and they don’t persist the data. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 56 Figure 2.12 PP/DS Fields in SAP S/4HANA Material Master: Table MARC The activation of advanced planning in the material master assigns the material to the active PP/DS model and version. The product master can be displayed in the PP/DS Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1. This is a display-only view, and no data maintenance is possible in the PP/DS transaction. All the basic MRP and advanced planning data objects maintained in the material master are visible in the PP/DS product master, as shown in Figure 2.13.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 57 2.3 Product Master Note Direct creation of material in embedded PP/DS isn’t possible for simulation purposes. Materials are always created and maintained in the ERP transaction and must be acti- vated for advanced planning. Materials are created and assigned to a plant in SAP S/4HANA, and the same assign- ment is available for the PP/DS product master data. Therefore, the location master data of the plant must be integrated before activating the material for advanced plan- ning. If an advanced planned material is assigned to an MRP area within the plant, the material can be planned in the MRP area in PP/DS as well.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, the MRP area should be integrated as a PP/DS location prior to activation of advanced planning. 2.3.2 Deactivation of Advanced Planning for Materials When a material is activated for advanced planning by setting the Advanced Planning indicator in the material master, and the material master is saved, in the PP/DS side, the material and the plant combination is created as a pegging area. Internally, the sys- tem generated a Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for the material/plant combination called a peg key , which identifies the pegging area and saves it in SAP liveCache.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP liveCache is object-based in-memory storage within the SAP HANA database where the embedded PP/DS data is replicated, so that the access to such data is faster. All the transaction data transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS is linked with the material/plant with the peg key. Apart from the transaction data, the peg key is also linked with the material-dependent master data such as the in-house source of supplies and external procurement relationships. When other transaction and master data is present in embedded PP/DS for a material, deactivation and removal of the Advanced Planning indicator will result in orphaned transactions and master data still being present in embedded PP/DS and in SAP live- Cache.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To avoid this inconsistent and orphaned data being present in embedded PP/DS, from the SAP S/4HANA 2020 release, the removal of the Advanced Planning indicator can’t be performed when dependent transaction data is present in embedded PP/DS. A new field called Planning Status was also introduced to control the activation and deac- tivation of materials for PP/DS, while the material remains integrated with PP/DS. To uncheck the Advanced Planning indicator in the material master, follow these steps: 1. Deactivate the material for advanced planning As shown in Figure 2.14, click on the Swap Planning Status button, which will change the status of the material from Active for planning to Marked for deactivation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 58 Figure 2.14 Marking Materials for Deactivation of Advanced Planning 2. Check for the presence of dependent data Click on the Where-Used Check button on the Advanced Planning tab in the material master, as shown in Figure 2.15. This will execute a where-used list for this material and search through all dependent master data and transaction data in PP/DS. If there is dependent master and transaction data in PP/DS, you’ll see a message, as shown in Figure 2.15, where references were found for a material in a plant.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When there are references in other master data objects found by the system, the Advanced Planning checkbox on the screen remains noneditable. In this case, exit the material master transaction. 3. Identify dependent data for PP/DS materials To identify dependent objects, execute Transaction WUF (Where-Used List), and select the Object Type 1 as Adv. Planning Location Product . The selection fields to enter the Product Number (material number) and the Location (plant) are then dis- played, as shown in Figure 2.16. Enter the product number and the location 2 , and click on the Execute 3 button.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the resulting screen, you’ll see the result of the where-used analysis. Click on the material number under the Obj. Name section 4 . This will load the list of objects 5 on the right side of the screen. In the example demonstrated in Figure 2.16, only orders are present in PP/DS for this material, so the LC Orders (SAP liveCache orders) tab is displayed. If other objects are present in PP/DS for this material, the corre- sponding objects such as PDSs will also be listed as tabs in the object list section. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 59 2.3 Product Master Clicking on the corresponding object will display the transaction or master data details in a table 6 . Figure 2.15 PP/DS Where-Used Check for Advanced Planning Materials Figure 2.16 Identification of the Dependent Data for Material/Plant in PP/DS Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 60 4. Delete material-dependent data in PP/DS Once the dependent transaction and master data objects are identified, several transactions and programs need to be executed to delete all such data objects. Table 2.1 shows the transactions and reports that can be used to delete the commonly used transaction and master data objects. 5. Remove the Advanced Planning indicator Go to the Advanced Planning tab of the material master in change mode. Click on the Where-Used Check button 1 , as shown in Figure 2.17.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As no dependent data exists in PP/DS, the Advanced Planning indicator 2 becomes editable. Remove the Advanced Planning checkbox, and save the material master. This will completely delete the material from PP/DS so that it can’t be accessed anymore from PP/DS. Tip After the materials are set Marked for Deactivation , execute report /SAPAPO/PPDS_ PPSKZ_RESET from Transaction SE38 or Transaction SA38 to execute a mass check for the where-used list and the dependency details. When this report is executed without simulation mode, if there are no dependencies identified, the system will uncheck the Advanced Planning indicator for such materials.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Navigating the details of the report logs will take you to the where-used list details dis- played in Transaction WUF. Object Transaction/Report to Delete the Data Planned orders Use heuristics SAP_INAC_05 to delete inactive planned orders or use the report /SAPAPO/OM_ DELETE_INCON_ORDERS for orders which are not deleted by the heuristics Planned independent requirements Transaction /SAPAPO/MD74 Stock elements Report /SAPAPO/DELETE_STOCK Sales orders Report /SAPAPO/SDORDER_DEL PDS (output is the inactive material) Transaction /SAPAPO/CULL_RTO_DEL PDS (the inactive material is the input) Retransfer the PDS using Transaction CURTOADV_ CREATE Transportation lanes Transaction /SAPAPO/TL1 and delete the material assignment to the transportation lane External procurement relationships Transaction /SAPAPO/PWBSRC2 Table 2.1 Delete Material-Dependent Data © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 61 2.3 Product Master Figure 2.17 Deactivation of the Advanced Planning Indicator in the Material Master 2.3.3 Advanced Planning Settings Specific to the Material Requirements Planning Area In the SAP S/4HANA material master, you can assign the materials to specific MRP areas. Typically, MRP areas are created to separate the planning of specific storage loca- tions from the plant. When MRP areas are created in the SAP S/4HANA system and assigned to the material master, if advanced planning is activated for the material, the system automatically activates the Advanced Planning indicator the MRP area level as well.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Warning When MRP areas are assigned to materials that are activated for advanced planning, the system automatically activates the advanced planning for the material in the MRP area as well. So, it’s mandatory to integrate the MRP areas as locations to PP/DS using program /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION before assigning advanced planning material to the MRP areas. If the MRP area location isn’t integrated to PP/DS, an error will be raised during the assignment of MRP areas to the materials. As shown in Figure 2.18, navigate to the MRP 1 view 1 of the material master, and click on the MRP Areas button 2 on the bottom of the screen.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 62 by double-clicking on the corresponding MRP Area 3 . PP/DS-specific settings can be maintained within the Advanced Planning tab 4 of the MRP area. Figure 2.18 Advanced Planning View in the MRP Area Although you can set the Advanced Planning status to Marked for deactivation in the MRP area level, you can’t remove the Advanced Planning checkbox from the MRP area. When the Advanced Planning checkbox is unchecked in the material master at the plant level, the Advanced Planning flag in the MRP area is also reset.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tip For mass copying of PP/DS fields in the advanced planning view from the plant level to the MRP area level, use program /SAPAPO/COPY_PLANT_TO_MRPAREA. This will only copy the PP/DS-relevant fields available in database table MDMA . 2.3.4 Flexible Integration of Material to Embedded PP/DS In the SAP S/4HANA material master, the concept of flexible integration is introduced from SAP S/4HANA release 2020. This provides flexibility for how a material is inte- grated into PP/DS by allowing you to choose the way the material is handled in PP/DS for planning and scheduling.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if you want to plan the material in a plan- ning system such as SAP Integrated Business Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP) and integrate the planning results to SAP S/4HANA and to embedded PP/DS, and you want embedded PP/DS to only perform scheduling, but not any planning, the flexible inte- gration options can be leveraged for such requirements. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 63 2.3 Product Master In the SAP S/4HANA material master under the Advanced Planning tab shown in Figure 2.19, the Scope Limitation field determines how the transaction data is integrated to PP/DS and what actions are possible within PP/DS when such scope limitation is defined. The Scope Profile field determines the list heuristics that are allowed to be executed in PP/DS with specific scope limitations. Figure 2.19 Scope Limitations in the Material Master for PP/DS Integration The scope profile is maintained under the SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Maintain Scope Profile .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 2.20, the default Scope Profile SAP_PPDS01 is delivered in the standard system. Select the scope profile 1 and navigate to the Allowed Heuristics Algorithms folder to display the list of heuristics algorithms 2 which are allowed to be executed for the materials, when the materials are assigned with this scope profile. You can copy the SAP_PPDS01 scope profile to another profile to add or remove heuristics algorithms which are allowed for your scope profile. The scope limitation can only be set when activating the Advanced Planning checkbox in the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the material is activated for advanced planning and saved, the Scope Limitation field becomes noneditable. So, to set a scope limitation or to change an already-set scope limitation, you must remove the Advanced Planning indi- cator, as described earlier in Section 2.3.2, and set the advanced planning again to make the Scope Limitation field editable. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 64 Figure 2.20 Scope Profile Configuration Settings There are four scope limitation options available. A blank value in this field means there are no limitations for integration of the transactional data from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS and also no restrictions on the interactive and background planning/scheduling functions and heuristics. The details on these scope limitations are described here:  PP/DS Display Only With this scope limitation, all the in-house procurement orders (e.g., planned orders, production orders, and process orders) and external procurement orders (e.g., pur- chase requisitions, stock transfer requisitions, purchase orders, and stock transfer orders) are integrated to PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But those will be only in display mode in PP/DS, so they can’t be changed or deleted in PP/DS. In addition, no order creation is possible in PP/DS for the materials with the PP/DS display only scope limitation. No planning functions can be executed in PP/DS using any of the planning and scheduling tools within PP/DS. In addition, no heuristics execution is possible in PP/DS © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 65 2.3 Product Master for planning or scheduling. This can be useful when materials planning is performed in external systems, no scheduling is required in PP/DS, and the orders need to be integrated to PP/DS for visibility purposes. As the execution of PP/DS heuristics isn’t allowed for this scope limitation, the Scope Profile field isn’t relevant, and no entry is allowed for the Scope Profile field.  PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only With this scope limitation option, external procurement orders are integrated to PP/DS as display-only orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These external procurement orders can’t be changed or deleted in PP/DS, and no external procurement order creation is possible in PP/DS. The system can only execute the heuristics that are listed under the scope profile assigned to the material master for PP/DS interactive planning tools such as the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) and scheduling tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPS0), as well as in background planning runs. The in-house procurement orders can be created, changed, and deleted in PP/DS interactively or via automatic planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When there is a scope limitation that restricts the functionality within PP/DS, a warning message is raised in interactive planning tools such as the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) to make you aware of the scope limitation, as shown in Figure 2.21. In background planning runs, warning and error logs are generated if a material can’t be planned or scheduled using a specific heuristic because it’s not part of the scope profile configuration. Figure 2.21 Warning on Scope Limitation in PP/DS Interactive Planning Tools This scope limitation can be applicable in scenarios where a mix of in-house and external procurement is possible for certain materials.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 66 determined in an external planning system, and you integrate the external procure- ment orders to PP/DS. Within PP/DS, you want the system to respect the sourcing decisions for external procurement. In addition, PP/DS needs to cover any un-covered demand with in-house procurement orders and schedule the in-house procurement orders with a restriction of the allowed heuristics for such materials.  PP/DS Restricted With this scope limitation option, you can create, change, and delete external and in-house procurement orders in PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For heuristics execution in PP/DS, you can only execute the heuristics that are listed in the scope profile. This scope limitation can be leveraged in scenarios where the planning is executed in external planning systems, but further planning functions—such as fixed peg- ging heuristics and scheduling heuristics—are to be executed within PP/DS. In such cases, those specific heuristics are assigned to the scope profile.  PP/DS Entire scope for Inhouse only This scope limitation option behaves exactly like PP/DS Restricted for In-house Only , but there are no limitations on the list of heuristics that can be executed in PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: So, the scope profile isn’t available to be filled with this scope limitation option. Tip When a material is present in multiple plants, program /SAPAPO/SCOPE_LIMITATION_ LIST can be used to list the scope limitation and scope profile of the material across plants and corresponding MRP areas. 2.4 Work Centers and Resources In this section, we’ll cover resource and work center data in SAP S/4HANA and how that data is integrated into PP/DS. We’ll also discuss the specifics of PP/DS resource master data. Resources and work centers represent the machines, tools, and labor resources that are used to manufacture products.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In industries that follow continuous or process manu- facturing (e.g., the chemical industry), the term resource is used to represent the pro- duction resources; in discrete manufacturing scenarios, the production resources are called work centers . Work centers and resources hold basic information about their usage in the production process, capacity definition, and scheduling data. In SAP S/4HANA, the data related to the activity types, which are used to derive the cost of the resource usage, plays a crucial role.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, the resource master data maintenance is simplified by eliminat- ing the need to create an integration model for transferring the work centers and resources to PP/DS. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 67 2.4 Work Centers and Resources 2.4.1 Work Centers Work centers are created in SAP S/4HANA by executing Transaction CR01 and are changed by executing Transaction CR02. After you execute Transaction CR01, enter a Plant , Work Center name, and Category , and then press (Enter) to arrive at the screen shown in Figure 2.22. In the Basic Data tab of the work center master data, select the Advanced Planning indicator. Figure 2.22 Activation of Advanced Planning in the SAP S/4HANA Work Center After the Advanced Planning indicator is selected, the resource is transferred to embed- ded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, the following four resource types are supported:  Single activity resource Only one activity can be performed in this resource at a given time. The available capacity is defined only as a dimension of time.  Multi-activity resource Multiple activities can be performed in this resource in parallel. The available capac- ity is defined as the time dimension, along with the number of individual capacities available. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 68  Production line Line resources are typically used in rate-based manufacturing such as automotive assembly lines.  Calendar resources These resources don’t hold any capacity, but they are used for determining the sched- ule of the activity performed in these resources. The handling resources that are assigned to the location master data to schedule the GR/GI processing times (inbound and outbound handling resources) are created as calendar resources. Although there is no need to schedule these handling activities based on any capaci- ties, a resource is still required in PP/DS to determine the schedule of those activities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PP/DS properties (e.g., resource type, category, validity of the resource time streams, etc.) are defaulted from the customizing maintained in Transaction CFC9 under the Initial Data Transfer and Change Transfer for Resource section, as shown in Figure 2.23. Figure 2.23 Default Values for PP/DS Resource Transfer The default values for the PP/DS resource properties, such as the resource type, cate- gory, and validity of the resource time stream, can be overwritten in the work center master data in SAP S/4HANA. You can use the APO Resource button in the capacity header of the work center master data from Transaction CR01 or Transaction CR02 to define the work center–specific PP/DS resource properties, as shown in Figure 2.24.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Resource Cat. (resource category) is a descriptive field for denoting the usage of the resource and doesn’t have a functional significance for scheduling. The time stream validity is determined by the fields Days - (days in past) and Days + (days in future), and the same is used to create the SAP liveCache time stream in PP/DS. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 69 2.4 Work Centers and Resources Figure 2.24 PP/DS Resource Properties in the SAP S/4HANA Work Center Note In the SAP S/4HANA work center, you’ll still see fields and resource types relevant to the standalone PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization sce- nario. In a side-by-side SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and SAP S/4HANA system, these resource types are still relevant, so they are still present but not relevant for embedded PP/DS. In the PPO Capacity Constraints tab, the relevant parameters for the Production Plan- ning Optimizer are maintained.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Production Planning Optimizer was introduced in SAP S/4HANA 2020 release and aids in achieving an optimal production plan. We’ll cover the details and functionality of the Production Planning Optimizer in Chapter 5, Section 5.8. After the work center is transferred to embedded PP/DS by setting the Advanced Plan- ning checkbox, the resource is available for maintenance of additional data in the PP/DS transaction. Execute Transaction /SAPAPO/RES01 to access the PP/DS resource master data. You can also follow SAP menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Resource  Resource , to access the resource master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because the resources are created in PP/DS, they are assigned to planning version 000. There is also a version-independent resource that is created in PP/DS. Certain pieces of PP/DS resource data, such as the classification of resources for characteristics- dependent planning (CDP), are maintained in the version-independent resource data. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 70 As shown in Figure 2.25, you can enter the Resource and the Location in the initial screen. In the Model and Plng Version section, enter the Planning Version “000” for the active version of the resource, or check the Model-Independent Selection checkbox to access the model-independent version of the resource. Click the Change Resources but- ton or the Display Resources button to change or display the resource details, respec- tively. Figure 2.25 Resource Master in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA: Initial Screen Tip When the work centers are transferred to embedded PP/DS, the work center name is prefixed with the letter “W”, and the suffix of the location and the capacity category is added.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, work center S4PPDS_W created in plant 0001 with capacity cate- gory 001 is created as WS4PPDS_W_0001_001 in PP/DS. In the details of the PP/DS resource, the resource and basic information is displayed in list form, when the Model-Independent Selection checkbox is set and the Planning Ver- sion is also set in the selection screen shown in Figure 2.25, the resource master data in version 000 and also the version-independent resource master are listed (see Figure 2.26 1 ) and the details are available in the individual tabs 2 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Under the PP/DS Bucket Cap. tab, there is an option to set the PP/DS bucket capacity, which is used for planning capacity at a daily or shift-wise buckets, but that isn’t valid for embedded PP/DS. The only bucket capacity supported in SAP S/4HANA is the block planning scenario bucket, which is set when the resource is enabled for block planning. We’ll cover more details about block planning in Chapter 8, Section 8.3.2, when discussing advanced PP/DS fea- tures. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 71 2.4 Work Centers and Resources Figure 2.26 PP/DS Resource Master Data: Details In the ExternalCap. tab, you can view the source of the capacity definition. If the External Capacity checkbox is selected, the capacity defined in the SAP S/4HANA work center is considered for the capacity definition. If the capacity definition needs to be maintained in embedded PP/DS, the External Capacity checkbox should not be selected. The downtimes or nonworking times due to planned or repair maintenance of the resources can be directly maintained in the Downtimes tab of the resource master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, when an SAP S/4HANA plant maintenance order can be integrated into PP/DS and a work center is assigned to the maintenance order, the maintenance duration is entered automatically as downtime in the PP/DS resource master. Specific fields such as the Setup Matrix shown in Figure 2.26 can be changed in the PP/DS resource master. Other settings for the resource are only maintained in the SAP S/4HANA work center under the APO Resource view under the capacity header, as shown earlier in Figure 2.24. Warning Clicking on the overview/details or (Ctrl) + (F8) in the resource displays the resource details in an overview list that enables you to change values for fields that aren’t edit- able in the detailed screen of the PP/DS resource master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Changing values here can cre- ate conflicts with the SAP S/4HANA work center master data, so don’t change any values in the overview option for fields available in the SAP S/4HANA work center APO Resource view. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 72 2.4.2 Resources In production planning for process industries in SAP S/4HANA (in SAP ERP, known as PP-PI) with process industry scenarios where continuous flow, processing, and storage vessels are required to be modeled in the master data, resources are created instead of work centers. One of the main differences between the resources and work centers is the category of the work center or the resource. In work center creation, you have the options to assign categories such as Machine , Labor , or Production Line .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In resources, you have categories such as Processing Unit , Storage Resources , and the combination of both, depending on the resource category. In this section, we’ll see examples of the Processing Unit and Storage Resource categories. Resources are created in the SAP S/4HANA system using Transaction CRC1 or via the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Production – Process  Master Data  Resources  Resource  Create . In the initial screen for resource creation, enter the Plant and a name for the Resource . Select the Resource category as 0015 – Proc. unit/Stor . res. , as shown in Figure 2.27.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 2.27 Resource Creation in Production Planning for Process Industries: Initial Screen In the next screen, fill in all required fields such as the Person Responsible and the Usage . The Stor. Loc. Res. , which represents the storage location, is assigned to the resource, as shown in Figure 2.28. For resources that can store materials, the inventory available in this assigned storage location is leveraged by PP/DS in the tank planning functionality. We’ll cover the details of tank planning in Chapter 8, Section 8.5. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 73 2.4 Work Centers and Resources For making the resource available in PP/DS, activate the Advanced Planning checkbox. Figure 2.28 Resource Creation in SAP S/4HANA Navigate to the Capacities tab, and click on the Capacity header . In the capacity header, click on the APO Resource button. As shown in Figure 2.29, navigate to the Storage Characteristics tab to enter the PP/DS storage properties of the resource. Activation of the Storage Characteristics checkbox defines the resource as a resource with storage capacity apart from the production capacity.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, the production capacity indicates that the resource has an availability of 24 hours, and the storage capacity indicates that the resource can also store a maximum of 10,000 gallons of liq- uids. As shown in Figure 2.29, enter the Storage Dimension , which is typically mass or vol- ume. Also enter a unit of measurement for the storage capacity ( Stock Unit ), along with the Min Production Qty (minimum production quantity, which must be filled for the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 74 storage resource) and the Maximum Stock Level of the storage resource. The Set Remaining Fill Level to Zero checkbox helps in ensuring product purity of the materials stored in the storage resource. For example, if Liquid 1 is to be filled in the storage resource, and that resource has Liquid 2 in storage already, with this flag set, the system sets the resource’s fill level to 0 and raises an alert in PP/DS to inform the scheduler that the resource contains another product. But if there is a small remaining quantity of the product in the storage resource that is under a certain value, the system is allowed to set the resource’s fill level to 0, and this value is maintained in the Threshold (Set Zero) field.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the Allow Multiple Products checkbox is switched on, the system allows multiple materials to be stored in the storage container at the same time. There- fore, this flag and Set Remaining Fill Level to Zero are mutually exclusive. Figure 2.29 Maintenance of Storage Characteristics in the Resource Master Data in SAP S/4HANA In the table under Time-Dependent Storage Data , Min. Production Qty , Maximum Stock Level , and Threshold (Set Zero) can be maintained in a time-phased manner. For exam- ple, if the maximum storage can be 10,000 gallons in the colder months, and the max- imum storage can only be 8,000 gallons in the warmer months, it can be achieved by the time-dependent storage data settings shown in Figure 2.29.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Resources that aren’t storage relevant are created with the Processing Unit resource category, and only the capacity details are maintained in the capacity header of the resource master in the SAP S/4HANA system. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 75 2.5 Sources of Supply 2.5 Sources of Supply In this section, we’ll cover the various sources of supply supported in the SAP S/4HANA system and how these can be transferred to PP/DS for their usage in planning. The sources of supply in embedded PP/DS refers to how the material will be produced or procured. For in-house production of products, the sources of supply in SAP S/4HANA include bills of material (BOMs), routings, and production versions, which combine the BOM and routing for a specific product. In addition, for the process industries, the mas- ter recipe is the in-house source of supply that comprises the manufacturing steps in the form of operations and phases in production and the BOM.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Materials that are procured externally from suppliers and materials transferred between plants, which are the external procurement sources of supplies in ERP sys- tems, include purchase info records, scheduling agreements, and contracts. 2.5.1 Production Data Structure For the in-house sources of supply in embedded PP/DS, the source of supply is called a production data structure (PDS), which contains all the basic, material, and scheduling information as defined in SAP S/4HANA BOMs, routings, and production versions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 2.30, the validity of dates, lot sizes for which this production version can be used, and the BOM and routing information are maintained in the production version master data. Figure 2.30 Production Version Master Data in SAP S/4HANA 2.5.2 Transfer of Routing to PP/DS as Production Data Structures Execute Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE to create the PDSs in embedded PP/DS by processing SAP S/4HANA master data. You can also navigate to SAP menu path, Logis- tics  Production  Master Data  PDS for Advanced Planning  PDS Transfer (PP/DS) , to execute the transfer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 76 The material for which the PDS is being transferred must be flagged for advanced plan- ning. If multiple material components are part of the BOM, only the material compo- nents flagged for advanced planning will be created as the components in the PDS data in embedded PP/DS. Similarly, the operations to which the work centers are assigned to the routing opera- tions must be flagged for advanced planning. Standard value key—the scheduling and capacity requirements formula—should be maintained in the work center data.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The routing operation must also have a nonzero activity time calculated during the sched- uling, and the control key assigned to the operation should allow scheduling. Note In SAP S/4HANA, it’s mandatory to have production versions for the consideration of BOMs and routings in the MRP run and source of supply determination. You can use report CS_BOM_PRODVER_MIGRATION02 to create production versions in an auto- mated manner. The selection screen of the PDS transfer is shown in Figure 2.31. The PDS must be avail- able in the PP/DS active version, so enter the value “000” for Pl.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Version in APO , and then enter the selection options for which you need to transfer the PDS to embedded PP/DS under Selection Criteria . PDSs are also used to manage the component requirements in the subcontracting sce- narios, where a product is manufactured completely or partly by a third-party vendor, and the plant sends the components to the vendor to complete the manufacturing pro- cess. In these cases, a production version for manufacturing is linked to the purchase info records or scheduling agreements, and the corresponding PDSs also can be created in embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can define the relevance of the PDS for the subcontracting scenario in the PDS Type section of the selection screen. You can see more options for the PDS transfer by scrolling down the screen, as shown in Figure 2.32. You can use the Extended Consistency Check checkbox to ensure the con- sistency of the PDS data in embedded PP/DS. Because this performance-intensive option does a lot of checks and validations, don’t use the Extended Consistency Check setting for transferring the PDS data periodically. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 77 2.5 Sources of Supply Figure 2.31 PDS Transfer to PP/DS: Selection Screen Figure 2.32 PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA: PDS Transfer Options When errors are generated in embedded PP/DS during the PDS transfer, the changes in master data aren’t transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. However, the PDS will continue to be used in the PP/DS planning. If you want to avoid this situation, select the Lock PDS in error case checkbox in the options. This will lock the PDS and avoid its usage in planning until the PDS integration is successfully completed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 78 Checking the Absolute Transfer checkbox to perform a complete transfer of the PDS data to PP/DS will regenerate the PDS based on the date from SAP S/4HANA. Conversely, the Change Transfer option is used for sending the changes made to SAP S/4HANA mas- ter data, such as BOMs, routings, and production versions, after the PDS is transferred to PP/DS. The transfer mode Absolute Transfer (Delta Mode) will create PDSs in PP/DS for newly created production versions in SAP S/4HANA, for example, if there are 10 PDSs that are already created in a plant for existing production versions and 3 new production ver- sions created in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When executing the PDS creation via Trans- action CURTOADV_CREATE, with Plant as the only selection option and with the transfer mode Absolute Transfer (Delta Mode) , this will only create the three new PDSs. With the transfer mode Absolute Transfer , it will send all 13 production versions to PP/DS for PDS generation. Tip Use Transaction CURTOADV_CRT_FOCUS for creating PDSs corresponding to order or work breakdown structure (WBS) BOMs in SAP S/4HANA. Because the WBS and order BOMs are specific to the sales order documents and WBS elements in the project sys- tem, a separate transaction is provided for selecting the order and WBS BOMs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PDS transfer can be executed in interactive mode using Transaction /SAPAPO/ CURTOADV_CREATE or can be scheduled as a background job with a selection variant defined for this transaction. The transfer logs are displayed immediately in the interac- tive mode, and the transfer log can be viewed from the application logs in background mode via Transaction SLG1 by entering “CIF” in the Object field. In embedded PP/DS, Transaction /SAPAPO/CURTO_SIMU is used to select and display the PDS data. As shown in Figure 2.33, after executing the transaction, you enter the Product Number , Location , and Planning Version in the selection screen to filter the PDS selection.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Additional selections are also possible by providing an Order Number in embedded PP/DS where the PDS is used. In addition, for the PDSs that have a specific account assignment, such as a sales order, the Special Stock and Account Assignment Element fields can be used for selection with the sales document number. These sales documents should be transferred before the PDSs are generated with reference to them. Click the Execute button to display the list of PDSs selected per the selection criteria provided. In the next screen, the list of PDSs is displayed, as shown in Figure 2.34.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To view the details, double-click on the corresponding PDS in the list. In the list view on the first section of the screen, the basic details from the SAP S/4HANA production version are displayed. The validity dates and lot sizes are copied from the production version data. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 80 The PDS details are shown in multiple sections and tabs, as shown in Figure 2.34:  Components All the material components that are transferred from the BOM linked to the pro- duction version are shown here. The header of the BOM is listed as an output com- ponent, and the components of the BOM are listed as input components.  Operations The operations that are relevant to PP/DS are transferred to this tab of the PDS. For master recipes, the operations and the phases under the operations are also listed here.  Activities One operation can contain multiple activities, such as the setup, production, and tear-down activities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The activities for all the operations are listed in this tab. The lot size dependency of the operation and also the base quantity defined in the opera- tion in the routing are transferred to the individual activities in the PDS. The dura- tion of the activities is calculated by the standard values for the activities defined in the routing operations.  Activity Relatshps The activities belonging to different operations form relationships in the PDS based on the relationships defined in the routing operations. For example, activities fol- lowing a sequence will have an end-start relationship.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The relationships of all the operations activities are listed in this tab.  Sequence Groups When parallel sequences are maintained in the routing, the sequence group infor- mation is listed in the Sequence Groups tab. The created modes are shown under the activities. The mode is the object in the PDS that holds the actual duration of the activity. As shown in Figure 2.35, the setup, prod- uct and teardown activities have their own modes, and the duration of the modes are calculated according to the SAP S/4HANA work center formula and the standard values maintained in the SAP S/4HANA routing.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The calculated value in the routings can be checked by executing the scheduling in the routing. During the PDS transfer to PP/DS, similar calculations are performed to determine the mode durations in the PDS. The mode durations are calculated with seconds as the unit of measure for the time. For checking the scheduling result of the routing in Transaction CA03, in the menu bar, select Extras  Scheduling  Schedule . The mapping of the operation durations based on the routing scheduling and the cor- responding values in the PDS modes is shown in Figure 2.35.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, the 10 min duration 1 for the produce activity (displayed as Edit in Figure 2.35 2 ) of the operation 0010 3 is shown as 600 seconds of mode duration 4 in the PDS under the Produce activity 5 . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 81 2.5 Sources of Supply Figure 2.35 Mapping of Mode Durations in PP/DS PDS from SAP S/4HANA Routings Tip When work centers in SAP S/4HANA are assigned with a class of type 019 with the same characteristics value, and if the routing operation is also assigned with the same class and the same characteristics value, during the PDS transfer all such work centers are created as alternative modes under the activity. For example, work centers WC1, WC2, and WC3 have class C1 and characteristics CHR1 with value of V1, and the routing operation is also assigned with Class CI with value V1 for the CHR1 characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this case, the PDS in PP/DS will have three alternative modes with WC1, WC2, and WC3 as possible resources under the activities generated from the routing operation. In embedded PP/DS, the PDS is only available for display, meaning the information can’t be changed. For the data that originates from the SAP S/4HANA master data (e.g., BOM, routing, and production version), the source of truth is the SAP S/4HANA master data, which can’t be changed in the PDS. However, some of the PP/DS PDS data can be maintained in Transaction PDS_MAINT in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Procurement priority of the PDS for the source of supply selection during the planning run or the costs associated with the individual PDSs can be main- tained in Transaction PDS_MAINT. After such PP/DS PDS data is maintained via the maintenance transaction, the PDS needs to be retransferred to embedded PP/DS using Transaction CURTOADV_CREATE to reflect the changes there. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 82 Tip When PDSs are copied into inactive planning versions (000 is the active planning ver- sion to which the PDS is integrated from SAP S/4HANA), Transaction /SAPAPO/CURTO_ EDIT can be used to edit the PDS. 2.5.3 Transfer of Master Recipes as Production Data Structures to PP/DS When production planning for process industries recipes is used in the SAP S/4HANA system for process manufacturing scenarios, the overall process of transferring the production version from SAP S/4HANA to a PDS in PP/DS remains similar to the trans- fer of routings to PP/DS as PDSs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But for the determination of the activities under the operations, a different method is used. The structure of the production planning for process industries master recipe is shown in Figure 2.36. Master recipes are created in the SAP S/4HANA system using Transaction C201. Unlike the routings, in master recipes, the operations have phases under them. For example, in a scenario where a chemical reaction operation of a manufacturing process is involved, and that operation requires 30 min of setup time to clean the reac- tor vessel and 1 hour of reaction time per 100 KG of materials, the recipe will have an operation 1 for Chemical Reaction under which phases 2 will be created.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The first phase is for the clean-up/setup time, and the second phase is created for the actual chemical reaction process. Figure 2.36 Structure of a Master Recipe in SAP S/4HANA For the PDS transfer to PP/DS, the setup phase will be identified by the assignment of a setup group to the phase of the master recipe. Phases with a setup group will become setup activities under the operation in the PDS, and other phases will be transferred as product activities. Apart from the setup group assignment to the phase in the master © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 83 2.5 Sources of Supply recipe, it’s also required to have a finish-start (FS) relationship between the setup and produce phases in the master recipe. The setup group needs to be integrated to PP/DS before the transfer of the PDS. Maintenance and integration of setup groups will be covered in Section 2.8. In the example shown in Figure 2.37, phase 0020 is assigned with a setup group 1 and has a FS relationship 2 with the phase 0030 . The mapping of this phase as a setup activity in the PDS is also shown in Figure 2.37.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The phase with the setup group assigned is created as a setup activity 3 , and the duration of the setup activity is set as 30 min (1,800 sec 4 ). Figure 2.37 Mapping of the Setup Phase to the Setup Activity between Master Recipe and PDS 2.5.4 External Procurement Sources of Supply In SAP S/4HANA, the sources of supply for external procurement include the following:  Purchase info records Purchase info records in the SAP S/4HANA system represent the purchasing relation- ship of a material with its supplier. The purchase info record contains the informa- tion-specific procurement lead times, quantity restrictions, and pricing conditions, which are valid for the material and the vendor.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The info records are defined at the purchasing organization level and can also have plant-level information. In addition, the info records can be classified as standard info records or subcontracting info records, among other types. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 84  Scheduling agreements Scheduling agreements are documents created at the plant level for procurement of material vendors on an agreed schedule. After the scheduling agreement is in place, the schedule line releases can be manually created, or the system can create sched- ule line releases via planning runs.  Contracts Contracts or outline agreements are documents created with a negotiated value or quantity of a material and follow-on purchasing documents such as purchase orders or schedule lines created to initiate the procurement.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, the purchase info records, contracts, and scheduling agreements are supported as external procurement relationships, which can be used by PP/DS planning to determine the source of supply. The transfer of the external procurement relationships to embedded PP/DS requires creation and activation of integration mod- els as of SAP S/4HANA 1909. As discussed in Section 2.2, an integration model is created using Transaction CFM1. You’ll arrive at the Create Integration Model screen, as shown in Figure 2.38.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter a name for the integration model in the Model Name field, and enter the Logical System and APO Application fields. The logical system in embedded PP/DS is the same as the logical system defined as the SAP S/4HANA system, as this is a self-system integration model generation. Figure 2.38 Creating the Integration Model for External Procurement Sources of Supply © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 85 2.5 Sources of Supply You may choose to create multiple integration models based on the plants or other fil- tering criteria (for object-specific selection, click the button) to manage the volume and to trigger retransfers periodically to embedded PP/DS. Under Material Dependent Objects , select the checkboxes for the relevant source of supplies. In the General Selection Options for Materials , enter the selection criteria with which the sources should be selected. In the Selection of Source of Supply section, select the Material-Dependent Source of Supply Selection checkbox to filter out the source of supplies per the selection entered in the General Selection Options for Mate- rials section.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Click on the Execute button to trigger the selection for the integration model. In the next screen, as shown in Figure 2.39, the sources of supplies are selected, and you can navigate to the selected sources by clicking on the count of the selected sources under the No. Filter Objs column. Click on the Generate IM button to complete the gen- eration of the integration model. Figure 2.39 Integration Model Generation in SAP S/4HANA After the integration model is generated, use Transaction CFM2 to activate the integra- tion model (refer to Section 2.1.2).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After entering the integration model details in the initial screen of Transaction CFM2, change the status of the integration model from Inactive to Active by clicking the X in the New Status box or by clicking on the Active/ Inactive button, as shown in Figure 2.40 1 . After the status is set as Active 2 , click on the Start button to start the transfer of data to embedded PP/DS. Queue failures may occur during this integration model activation. In interactive mode, where you execute the activation of the integration model as explained in this section, the queue errors are displayed on the screen.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In background mode, the queues should be analyzed from the queue monitor to troubleshoot the errors and reprocess them. It’s also possible to activate the integration model in background mode by using ABAP program RIMODAC2. We’ll cover queue monitoring and troubleshooting in Chapter 10 for administration of embedded PP/DS. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 86 Figure 2.40 Activation of the Integration Model for External Sources of Supply After the integration model is activated, and the queues are successfully processed, the external sources of supplies are available for PP/DS planning. These sources are called external procurement relationships in embedded PP/DS and can be accessed using Transaction /SAPAPO/PWBSRC1 or from SAP menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  External Procurement Relationship  Display . The Change External Procurement Relationships screen appears, as shown in Figure 2.41.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the left part of the screen, the procurement relations are listed per the selection criteria and are grouped by the type of procurement relationship. Double-click on the item number of any procurement relationship to display the details of the specific source. In the General Data section, the organizational data ( Purchasing Org. , Dest. Loc. [plant]) and the basic information (validity dates and source/destination locations) are displayed. The Source Loc. is the location of the vendor, and the Dest. Loc. is the location of the receiving plant.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 87 2.5 Sources of Supply You can click on the Display<->Change button to make the sources editable. To over- write the planned delivery time sent from SAP S/4HANA, the Plnd Del. Time is an edit- able field, and the source can be made active or inactive by selecting the Ext. proc. relationship active checkbox under the Settings section. As you can see in Figure 2.41, there is an Assigned Transportation Lanes sequence in the sources. Transportation lanes are master data generated by the system during the transfer of external procurement sources to embedded PP/DS and are assigned to the corresponding products.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The procurement parameters also can be maintained at the transportation lane, and a mode of transport can be assigned to the transportation lane to ensure that the exact dates are calculated during planning for the procurement and transportation of materials from the vendor to the receiving plants. You can execute Transaction /SAPAPO/TL1 to display or change the transportation lanes. In the selection screen of this transaction, enter the Model Name “000”, which is the active PP/DS model, and all the transportation lanes integrated via the source of supply integration model are always created in the 000 model.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, enter the Start Location and Dest. Location , as shown in Figure 2.42. Figure 2.42 Transportation Lanes in PP/DS: Selection Screen Choose Display or Change , depending on the action you want to perform, and the details of the transportation lane are displayed in the next screen. As shown in Figure 2.43, the products and the procurement relationships using the same transportation lanes are listed in the top section of the screen 1 . Selecting one of the sources will dis- play the details of the procurement on the right side of the screen; in change mode, the information specific to PP/DS can be edited and isn’t transferred back to SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A means of transport, such as rail, truck, or air, and the corresponding data can be maintained by creating a new means of transport under the Means of Transport sec- tion 2 , where the means of transport common to all products in the transportation lane are located. You can also define multiple means of transport and assign specific means to specific products 3 . Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 88 Figure 2.43 Details of Transportation Lanes in PP/DS 2.6 Classes and Characteristics In this section, we’ll discuss the usage of classes and characteristics in embedded PP/DS as well as how the classes and characteristics are maintained in the system. A character- istic denotes a specific attribute of a product, such as color, capacity, usage, and so on. Characteristics that define a set of attributes of a product are grouped under a class. In PP/DS planning, there are two ways to use the classification system:  Characteristics - dependent planning (CDP) CDP is used in in-house manufacturing processes to match the characteristics of the demand element, such as sales order or dependent demand, to a supply element that has the same characteristics value assignment (also called characteristics valua- tion).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The CDP scenario supports both make-to-stock (MTS) and make-to-order (MTO) planning scenarios.  Variant configuration (VC) VC is used for complex configurable products mainly in MTO scenarios where the specification of the product in the sales order drives the manufacturing processes. Either in CDP or VC scenarios, the classes and characteristics play the major role in transferring the configuration of the product from the demand level to the manufac- turing level. Class types are defined in the SAP S/4HANA system to allow them to be © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 89 2.6 Classes and Characteristics used in a specific scenario. We’ll cover the configuration schema (CDP versus VC) of the PP/DS system in Chapter 3 when we discuss configuration. You can execute Transaction CT04 to create, change, and delete characteristics master data, as shown in Figure 2.44. Figure 2.44 Maintenance of Characteristics Master Data The Basic data fields, such as the Description and Status of the class, are maintained in the Basic data tab, and the allowed values for this characteristic can be maintained in the Values tab.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For complex configuration scenarios, a cross-reference to a specific table reference can be done in the Addnl data tab. Classes are created using Transaction CL01 and can be maintained from Transaction CL02. The characteristics are assigned to the class. Class of type 300 is used in VC scenarios, and the same is available for PP/DS in the VC scenario. There is no need to create an integration model for making the class of type 300 to be available for PP/DS. The class assignment to the material in the VC scenario is done in the SAP S/4HANA material master in the classification view, and the same can be displayed in embedded PP/DS when the material is marked for advanced plan- ning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Master Data 90 Figure 2.45 Display of Classification Data in the PP/DS Product Master From the Classification tab, click on the Classes button to display the classes assigned to the material master, which is visible to PP/DS. Here, you can see Class Type 300 . When the configuration schema is set to CDP in embedded PP/DS, class types 023 (batch class) and 300 (variant class) need to be integrated into embedded PP/DS. This will create a new class with type 400 (CDP class) with the same class name in embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To integrate the classes of type 023 and 300 using an integration model, follow these steps: 1. Define an organizational area in the Customizing Transaction O1CL. In this transac- tion, select the entry for MARA , and select the Organizational Areas folder, as shown in Figure 2.46. Make entries for the relevant class types, and enter an organizational area (in the O column). Organizational area can be any character with one-character length. docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This can be for both in-house manufacturing sources of supplies for in-house manufacturing and external procure- ment sources of supply for external procurement. When multiple sources of supplies are available, the quota arrangement master data is used to determine what portion of the demand is fulfilled by which source. For the in- © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 93 2.7 Quota Arrangements house production scenario, the quota can allocate the demand quantities between available PDSs. For example, if there are two manufacturing lines represented by two different PDSs in PP/DS, and if you want to allocate 70% of the demand to line 1 and 30% of the demand to line 2, this can be achieved by setting up the quota arrangement master data. Similarly for external procurement, where there are multiple vendors sup- plying the same material and you want to split the demand between these available vendors in a certain percentage allocation, quota arrangement can help.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, if there are stock transfer scenarios, such as two plants that can supply the material to one plant, and you want to allocate the demand to the supplying plants in certain per- centages, the quota arrangement can be leveraged by assigning the percentage alloca- tion between the transportation lanes of these locations. In the embedded PP/DS system, the quota arrangement master data is created using Transaction /SAPAPO/SCC_TQ1 or the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Master Data  Quota Arrangement  Quota Arrangement .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The changeover duration and cost are typically based on the characteristics of the product being produced in the relevant operation. In this section, we’ll cover the details of the static setup matrix and the PP/DS generated setup matrix, which are based on the characteristics assigned to the products. In embedded PP/DS, the setup matrix is used to determine the changeover time between two operations on a resource. For example, if black paint and white paint are being packaged on the same packing line, and after a production order is executed for packing black paint, the packaging line needs a thorough cleaning before the white paint order is started.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If this cleaning process takes 30 minutes (min), the changeover time from the black paint order to white paint order is 30 min. There can also be more complex changeover situations. In the preceding example, apart from the color transition, if there are multiple sizes of packed products being packed, for example, 50 grams (g), 100 g, and 500 g packaging, and they have their own changeover time to unload and reload the packaging materials to the lines, it makes the possible combinations of transitions complex. The changeover of 50 g black to 100 g black may just take 5 min because only the packaging material needs to be changed, whereas the changeover from 50 g black to 100 g white will take 30 min for cleaning and 5 min for loading the new packaging material.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, if the cleaning and the loading of packaging material is performed in parallel, the changeover will be 30 mins, but if these tasks are done sequentially, the changeover will be 35 min (30 min for cleaning and 5 min for loading). These possible combinations for changeovers are typ- ically maintained in a matrix. To address such simple and complex transitions in the embedded PP/DS solution, there are two setup matrix options provided:  Conventional setup matrix (static setup groups)  Generated setup matrix (dynamic setup groups) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 97 2.8 Setup Matrix 2.8.1 Static Setup Matrix In the static setup matrix, the setup groups are the conditions for the changeovers. For example, all black paint products are in setup group Black, and all white paint products are in setup group White. These groups are assigned in the corresponding operation within the routing. If there are some exceptions within the group, for example, if the packet size needs to be transitioned from 50 g to 500 g, which takes an additional 15 min of changeover time, setup keys with the setup groups can help with that.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The setup groups and setup keys are created in the SAP S/4HANA system and assigned to the routing operations. The setup groups and setup keys need to be transferred to the embedded PP/DS system via an integration model. Then, the transfer of routing from SAP S/4HANA to the embedded PP/DS PDS will assign the corresponding setup groups to the PDS operations and activities. To create the setup groups and keys in the SAP S/4HANA system, follow the IMG menu path, SPRO  Production  Capacity Requirements  Planning  Master Data  Routing Data  Define Setup Parameters .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA

Select the setup group name, and double-click on the Setup group key . Click on the New Entries button, and enter the setup key values. Similarly, enter the setup group and keys for all required transition scenarios. Figure 2.52 Configuration of Setup Groups and Keys in SAP S/4HANA Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

For example, in the food industry, the characteristics of a product include kosher versus nonkosher products, products containing allergens versus nonallergen-containing products, different flavors of the food being produced, or different packaging sizes.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Cre- ating setup groups and keys for the preceding mentioned possible combinations (e.g., changeover from kosher-allergen-savory 10 oz pack to kosher-nonallergen-savory 10 oz pack takes 30 min of changeover time) and assigning them in the master recipe phases would be almost an impossible task. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 101 2.8 Setup Matrix To handle such requirements in embedded PP/DS, you can use the generated setup matrix. The generated setup matrix works based on the classification of the product itself, and the system generates the combinations for the changeovers. There is no need to assign the setup groups to the routings or master recipe operations, as the sys- tem reads the classification data of the material to determine the setup group dynami- cally and derives the changeover (setup) times from the setup matrix. We’ll consider an example of products requiring setup time determination based on two characteristics: color and pack size.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: COLOR has the characteristics values of BLACK, WHITE, and RED. PCKSIZE (pack size) has the values of 50, 100, and 500 g. Each of these characteristics will have 9 possible transitions, and, as shown in Figure 2.56, both char- acteristics will form a possibility of 81 combinations. Figure 2.56 Possible Setup Transitions Based on Characteristics In PP/DS, we’ll achieve the same matrix by following these steps: 1. Create the classification and integrate to PP/DS Create characteristics/class of type material class (001), assign them to the material master in SAP S/4HANA, and integrate the class and characteristics to embedded PP/DS via the integration model.
