docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 71 2.3 Summary 2.3 Summary This chapter explained the importance of mapping most (if not all) of the important actual business processes of a company in the SAP S/4HANA system during the sys- tem’s implementation. We also highlighted the importance of the enterprise structure of not just PP but of the entire organization, along with interdependencies. The refer- ence table acts as an invaluable guide to understanding the importance of several PP- specific configuration elements, such as MRP controllers, production schedulers, and capacity planners.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 75 Chapter 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration Implementing discrete manufacturing, also known as shop floor control (SFC), involves a series of logical and sequential configuration steps to ensure complete mapping of configuration with the business processes of the company. During an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, once it’s established that discrete manufacturing will most closely serve the business needs of the company, the next logical step is to have intensive discussions and several workshops to help team mem- bers agree on the configuration objects of discrete manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Configuration of the discrete manufacturing production type forms the basis on which the business pro- cesses of the company will run. For example, how should the system behave when it comes across a material or capacity shortage during production order creation or release? How should it behave when the actual production exceeds the defined under- delivery or overdelivery of the material? What should the system do if it’s unable to schedule production within the defined basic dates? For each of these (and many more) questions, you can set controls on the degree of freedom or flexibility (or strictness) that will enable the system to allow or disallow certain options when users are perform- ing relevant business functions.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, the system can be configured to allow a user to create a production order despite a component shortage but to stop a user from releasing it until the requisite components for production are available in stock. In this chapter, we begin by covering the configuration basics needed to set up the mas- ter data used in discrete manufacturing. Then, we follow a step-by-step process to cre- ate a new production order type, PP10, including assigning it a new number range. The subsequent configuration steps covered for this order type and in this chapter are suf- ficient to enable a business user to set up master data and then run end-to-end busi- ness processes in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Chapter 6 will cover the master data setup and the business processes side of the configuration undertaken in this chapter. If, as an SAP consultant or a business process owner, this is your first time configuring and implementing PP, we suggest following the step-by-step approach in this chapter. Because PP integrates with several other functional areas, such as MM, quality manage- ment (QM), and, most importantly, product cost controlling, we suggest that you main- tain close coordination throughout by consulting the resources of these functional- ities.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 76 Note The business processes of discrete manufacturing and process manufacturing are also similar in a lot of ways. Any differences are specifically covered in the relevant chapters (process manufacturing is covered in Chapter 4). Note Refer to Chapter 1 for a features comparison among discrete manufacturing, process manufacturing, and REM, as well as to learn how to decide which manufacturing type is most relevant for a given industry. 3.1 Material Master The configuration of the material master is primarily managed within MM.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: During an SAP S/4HANA system implementation, the MM team coordinates with the client to dis- cuss and agree on a large number of MM-specific configuration objects, which also include material types. A material type is a unique identification to distinguish materi- als used in various business processes. Some examples of material types are raw mate- rials, semifinished goods, trading materials, packing materials, nonvaluated materials, spare parts, and consumables. However, the importance and involvement of PP can’t be overemphasized here because the MRP and work scheduling views of the material master are very important to PP, from both a planning perspective and an execution perspective.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PP information is maintained in the MRP views of the material master to enable the system to perform reliable material planning. The work scheduling view controls how production execution should take place. Apart from the option for quantity and value updates, it’s also possible to control the views that the system makes available to the end user during material master creation. For example, the purchasing view isn’t normally available for finished goods because the company doesn’t purchase finished goods. Similarly, for raw materials, the sales views aren’t available because the company normally doesn’t sell its raw materials.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To set up the material type attributes, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Material Master  Basic Settings  Material Types  Define Attributes of Material Types . Figure 3.1 shows the configuration view of Material Type FERT ( Finished Product ). In the lower-right side of the screen, you can select the option to control the views that the system makes available during material master. At the bottom of the screen (not shown) is the Price Control field, which lets you select whether the material will have a moving average price or a standard price. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 77 3.2 Bill of Materials Figure 3.1 Material Types 3.2 Bill of Materials Similar to the material master, a material’s BOM is used extensively in various areas of the supply chain, including planning, production, sales, and costing. A BOM is a for- mally structured list of components that is needed to produce a material. These com- ponents may be raw materials or packing materials procured directly from vendors or subassemblies produced in house. The BOM has a large number of functions. A user can have a BOM that is specific to engineering/design only, whereas another BOM of the same material can be used for costing purposes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There can be a production BOM and also a sales BOM. In a sales BOM , the system “explodes” the components and makes them an integral part of sales pro- cessing. For example, when a company sells a new car, it also includes accessories, such as a spare tire, a tire-changing toolkit, and an owner’s manual, among other things. These accessories are, in fact, components in a sales BOM. A material BOM is a central component in MRP. When the system runs the MRP on a material, it looks for its BOM to plan not just at the finished goods level but also at the components level and raw materials level.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The material BOM is always a single level and can be exploded and displayed as a cascade of BOMs in a multilevel structure. The system displays a single-level BOM by showing its immediate next component or assembly. In a multilevel BOM, the system reflects comprehensive details of all the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 78 assemblies, the components, the associated quantities of assemblies and components, and their logical relationships to each other. In the following sections, we’ll cover the various business functions and controls avail- able for BOMs, including maintaining the various statuses of a BOM and allowing or disallowing certain material types’ usage in a BOM. 3.2.1 Defining Bill of Materials Usages A BOM’s usage controls the activities and functions that the system can perform in business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There can also be a separate BOM usage for long-term planning or predictive material resource planning (pMRP) to simulate the materials and capacity requirements for a given business scenario. To create a new BOM usage, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  General Data  BOM Usage  Define BOM Usages or use Transaction OS20. Here, several standard BOM usages are available. Create a new BOM usage by choosing New Entries and selecting the control functions to allow or disallow the business pro- cesses in which the BOM usage is applicable (see Figure 3.2).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.2 BOM Usages 3.2.2 Allowed Material Types in the Bill of Materials Header It’s possible to control the material types that the system allows for creation of a mate- rial BOM. For example, normally, creating a material BOM for spare parts or consum- able material types isn’t required. This control on material types for BOM creation also helps prevent the creation of unnecessary or unwanted material BOMs. During the SAP © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 79 3.2 Bill of Materials project, if several company-specific material types are configured by the MM consul- tant, then they must be specifically identified and perform the necessary configuration for all of the material types that will have any BOM usage. To specify the material types for a material BOM creation, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Bill of Material  General Data  Define Material Types Allowed in BOM Header or use Transaction OS24. Figure 3.3 shows that the BOM usage for the material type at the header level can be specified.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The * symbol denotes that a BOM can have all usage types and can also be used in all material types at the header level. Figure 3.3 Allowed Material Types in BOM Header Note In addition to maintaining the control function of the material type at the BOM header level, it’s possible to do the same for a material at the BOM item level. To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Bill of Material  Item Data  Define Material Types Allowed for BOM Items or use Transaction OS14. 3.2.3 Bill of Materials Status Different applications of a material BOM based on its status can be controlled.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, during new product development, a material has a BOM status of Engineer- ing/Design . When the engineering/design departments approve it, the next status can Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 80 be Costing , which enables the product costing team to calculate the cost of the material. Finally, when the costing department also approves the material BOM, it can attain the status of Production , which enables the production team to begin producing the mate- rial. When the BOM has a Production status, it becomes available during production order creation, whereas when its status is either Engineering/Design or Costing , it isn’t available in production order creation. You can also have a BOM status in which all these functions are possible, such as BOM status 1 .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create or set the BOM status, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  General Data  Define BOM Status or use Transaction OS23. Figure 3.4 shows the option to control whether the BOM status should allow business functions, such as being available during MRP explosion, for costing, or for work scheduling (production). Figure 3.4 BOM Statuses 3.2.4 Bill of Materials with History Requirement It’s possible to control whether changes made to the material BOM are with reference to a change number or engineering change management.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With a history requirement or change number, the system requires you to enter the change number before it allows you to make the desired changes. This adds a level of security. To select the BOM usage and status combination for which there’s a need to set the his- tory requirements, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  General Data  Configure History Requirement for BOMs or use Transaction OS25. On the screen that appears, mark the required BOMs with a history requirement by checking their boxes. 3.2.5 Item Category in Bill of Materials The item category provides further divisions of the different BOM classes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: While some item categories are relevant for production or planning, others are there merely to pro- vide information. The following are some of the most important predefined item cate- gories:  L: Stock item Stock items contain components that are stored in a warehouse and included as a part of inventory management (IM). © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 81 3.2 Bill of Materials  N: Nonstock item A nonstock item is a material that isn’t available in stock but is procured directly for the given production order. A nonstock item has a direct relationship to the procure- ment process. There is also no need to have a material master (item code) for a non- stock material. If a nonstock material is used, then you must also fill in the procure- ment details, such as cost element, purchasing group, material group, and price.  R: Variable-size item In this item category, a formula is used to define the sizes of the variables to enable the system to perform calculations and suggest the component’s quantity.  T: Text item The text item has a descriptive character.  M: Intra material This item category is commonly used in master recipes (process industry).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Materials that are temporarily used in process engineering are recorded as components with this item category. The material input parameter ( MatInpt ) indicates whether a material reference to the item exists. This isn’t the case with document items or nonstock items. The IM param- eter ( InvMg ) allows you to set that up to only use those materials whose quantities are managed in IM. To maintain a new item category or make changes to the existing ones, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Item Data  Define Material Types Allowed for BOM Header or use Transaction OS24.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Check or uncheck the boxes to meet your business needs. 3.2.6 Variable-Size Item Formulas In the fabrication industry, components issued to produce an assembly are often based on a formula. For example, to produce the fuel tank of a motorcycle, the warehouse issues the steel sheet based on the formula, which calculates the requirement. When you’re assigning a variable-size item in the BOM of the material with item category R, the system gives you the option to enter the variable-size details in the relevant area of the BOM’s item details area.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note Before you create a formula for a variable-size item, you can define a unique unit of measure to denote the formula via Transaction CUNI. To create a variable-size item formula, follow the SAP S/4HANA system menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Item Data  Define Variable-Size Item Formula or use Transaction OS15. Figure 3.5 shows the list of available formulas that you can use, or you can create a new one. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 82 Figure 3.5 Variable-Size Item Formulas 3.2.7 Bill of Materials Explosion Types It’s possible to control how the system takes a specific component’s explosion into account in the Basic Data view of the BOM creation screen. This control allows you to set whether direct production or a phantom assembly is deactivated. You can set its explosion type status in the Basic Data view of the material’s component, and if you don’t find the desired configuration settings, then you can configure them using menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Item Data  Define Explosion Types . 3.2.8 Bill of Materials Selection (Order of Priority) It’s possible to control how the system makes an automatic selection of a BOM to incor- porate it into, say, a planned order during an MRP run.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, during the MRP run, if the system is unable to find a material’s BOM for production (BOM usage 1), then you can select the next BOM selection priority that is set as universal (BOM usage 3). To configure the BOM selection and its order of selection priority, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Bill of Materials  Alternative Determination  Define Order of Priority for BOM Usages or use Transaction OS31. Here, you can define the selection ID to combine all BOMs with one unique ID. Then, you can define the selec- tion priority of each BOM and finally assign the BOM usage, such as production or uni- versal. 3.3 Work Center A work center is a machine or a group of machines, a person or a group of persons, or a group of persons and machines that adds value to the manufacturing process.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: During an SAP implementation project, the production team and the product costing team discuss and mutually agree on the number of work centers that needs to be available. The decision is primarily focused on ensuring that the production department can schedule and plan work centers and machine capacities, whereas the product costing team ensures that the reporting for both activities and cost centers is available. For © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 83 3.3 Work Center example, if the packaging process incurs significant costs that the product costing team needs to monitor, then it makes sense to create a packaging work center and assign a separate cost center and associated activities to it. If these costs don’t require separate monitoring, then the production line cost center is sufficient. In the following sections, we explain how to make field selections in the work center so that during creation of the work center, the system makes a field entry either manda- tory or optional.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We also discuss how to use a standard value key to define which activ- ities are important for an operation from a business perspective. We discuss defining formulas for the work center that can be used in capacity requirements planning, scheduling, and costing, and we also discuss location groups to account for the time it takes to move a product from one work center to another and the corresponding sys- tem to consider this during scheduling. Finally, we discuss using a control key for oper- ations as a control function to decide if, for example, scheduling or printing for an operation is allowed. 3.3.1 Work Center Category A work center category is a control function that ensures which master data applica- tions and business processes of discrete manufacturing the work center can be used in.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, work center category 0007 is available for rate routing in REM, and in this category, the available application option for REM can be found. In the same way, work center category 0008 is available and used for process manufacturing, and in this cate- gory, the master recipe application can be found. To create a work center category, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  General Data  Define Work Center Category or use Transaction OP40. Select work center category 0001 used in discrete manufacturing and double-click the Application folder.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The available applications in the resulting screen are shown in Figure 3.6 for Cat. (category) 0001 . Figure 3.6 Application of Work Center Category Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 84 3.3.2 Field Selection in the Work Center It’s possible to control the fields in the SAP system for which entry is mandatory, optional, an input option, or hidden from display. For example, during work center cre- ation, if a user must enter information in a specific field, then selecting the Req. radio button will ensure a mandatory entry. When a user enters information in one field, the system can also control prompting the user or preventing the user from performing any dependent function.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This option works when one modifiable field relates to the influencing fields. For this example, if a user selects work center category 0001 as an influencing field, the system makes the Backflush field indicator (a modifiable field) a mandatory entry. So, whenever a user creates a work center with category 0001, select- ing the Backflush field is also mandatory. Note The field selection option isn’t just restricted to work centers; it can also be used in BOMs, routings, and confirmations. To define field selection in a work center, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  General Data  Define Field Selection or use Transaction OPFA.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.7 shows that the Basic data screen group has several modifiable fields, such as Backflush or Person Responsible . Figure 3.7 Modifiable Fields of Basic Data Screen Group © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 85 3.3 Work Center Five options are available in the modifiable fields:  Input Making an entry in this field is optional.  Req. (required) Making an entry in this field is mandatory.  Disp. (display) There’s no entry in this field because it’s available for display only.  Hide The system hides this field, and it isn’t displayed.  HiLi (highlight) Any specific field can be highlighted for the user’s attention. For example, when marking a field entry as Req. , you can check the HiLi box to enable the user to quickly see the fields requiring entries.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Double-click the Backflush field or click the Modified button. In the screen that appears, as shown in Figure 3.8, click the New values button. In the popup that appears, enter the work center category as “0007” and click Continue . Click the Req. radio button to ensure that whenever a user creates a work center of category 0007, clicking the Back- flush indicator is mandatory. Figure 3.8 Modifiable Field with Influences Do the same with work center category 0014 , but this time, click the Hide radio button. The system won’t show the Backflush field when the user creates a work center with work center category 0014.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 86 3.3.3 Formulas for the Work Center The system uses previously defined parameters to define formulas that can then be used in capacity requirements planning or scheduling. The following parameters can be used:  SAP_08 Base quantity  SAP_09 Operation quantity  SAP_11 Number of operation splits A formula definition also holds the control for the following functions:  Capacity requirements planning  Scheduling  Costing To define the formula parameter, if it’s different from the ones already available, use menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  Costing  Work Center For- mulas  Define Formula Parameters for Work Centers or use Transaction OP51.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To define the formula that can be used in the work center for costing, capacity require- ments planning, and scheduling, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  Costing  Work Center Formulas  Define Formula for Work Centers or use Transaction OP54. In Figure 3.9, notice the formulas for calculating the production processing duration. Figure 3.9 Formula Definition in Work Center © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 87 3.3 Work Center The system calculates the capacity requirement as follows: Capacity requirement = Standard value × Order quantity ÷ Base quantity The processing duration can be reduced if the operation is processed simultaneously at several work centers, per the following formula: Duration = Standard value × Order quantity ÷ Base quantity ÷ Number of splits In Chapter 6, these formulas will be assigned in the Scheduling , Capacities , and Costing tabs of a work center. Figure 3.10 shows the ZPOWER Formula Key and the associated Formula that also uses the ZPOWER parameter in formula calculation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This ZPOWER formula key is then assigned to a standard value key. Figure 3.10 Self-Defined ZPOWER Parameter Used in Formula Key 3.3.4 Standard Value Key During the course of an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, one of the main areas where the production and product costing teams collaborate is in defining the stan- dard value key, which consists of individual parameters that are then grouped together as one standard value key. The standard value key is assigned in the Basic Data view of the work center and also entered in the formula that the system will use for each of the parameters.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following sequence of steps is used to define a standard value key: 1. Define the parameters. 2. Assign the parameters to the SVK. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 88 3. Create a formula for the work center. 4. Assign a formula against each parameter. Let’s explain this with an example. Suppose that in addition to monitoring and record- ing standard durations, such as setup, machine, and labor, your product costing depart- ment wants to record the electricity and steam consumed in producing a product. The reason to record these two unique parameter values is that a significantly high cost is associated with them. For example, in the caustic soda industry, electricity consump- tion (power) is excessive and is closely monitored, so it’s a critical cost component that the company wants to monitor and control.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, in the steel rerolling industry, electricity and natural gas constitute significant costs of the finished product and therefore must be recorded and monitored. When determining the parameters to use and monitor for a standard value key, you should confirm with the company whether these parameters are quantifiable and measurable for recording in the SAP S/4HANA system. When the user uses a specific work center (or resource) consisting of the standard value key in the routing (or master recipe), the system requires the user to enter the standard consumptions.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this example, in the routing, the system prompts the user to define the standard electricity consumption to produce one metric ton of caustic soda. The product costing team will also have an associated cost (in the form of an activity type) assigned to this parameter (electricity). When the user performs the confirmation against the process order and enters the actual electricity consumed, the production team and product costing team can monitor the variances between standard con- sumption and actual consumption.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Up to six parameters can be assigned to a standard value key. In other words, up to six important parameters that have direct cost implications for a given work center can be monitored and recorded. Standard value keys can also be used in scheduling and capac- ity calculations. To define a parameter, use menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  General Data  Standard Value  Define Parameters or use Transaction OP7B. The initial screen consisting of standard and user-defined parameters will be displayed, and when you double-click SAP_02 , the screen shown in Figure 3.11 will appear.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The standard parameter with TIME as a Dimension and Standard Value Unit in MIN (minutes) will then be displayed. If you’re creating a self-defined parameter, such as power, steam, or elec- tricity, then give the dimension and the unit of measure in which to record the con- sumption value. Next, to create the standard value key, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  General Data  Standard Value  Define Standard Value Key or use Transaction OP19 or OPCM. Figure 3.12 shows the Std Value Key SAP1, which consists of the standard parameters SAP_01 , SAP_02 , and SAP_03 .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 89 3.3 Work Center previously, up to six parameters can be maintained in a standard value key. Make sure to check the Generate box when defining a standard value key because then, the sys- tem will automatically perform the calculations defined in the formulas. Otherwise, it will do the calculation for scheduling and capacity planning during production order creation, which often leads to system performance issues. Figure 3.11 Machine Standard Parameter with Unit of Measure Figure 3.12 Standard Value Key Formula Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 90 Figure 3.13 shows an example of a self-defined standard value key, ZCL1, which contains two parameters (machine hours and teardown hours) that a cladding manufacturing company wants to record, monitor, and make part of its product costing. Figure 3.13 Self-Defined Standard Value Key Containing Self-Defined Parameters 3.3.5 Location Groups A location group consists of a physical location where each work center is located. Sev- eral work centers can be combined into one location group if they are in close proximity to one another.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can use the move time matrix to provide standardized values for different transition times (also known as interoperation times ), such as queue time, wait time, and move time. If there’s no business need to use the move time matrix, then maintain this transition time information either in the work center or in the routing. The location group is assigned to the work center, and in the move time matrix, you define the normal and minimum move times between locations. The system uses the working times maintained in the move time matrix for scheduling the move times.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Basically, two steps are performed: 1. Maintain the location groups. 2. Maintain the matrix of move times from one location group to another. To set up location groups, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Work Center  General Data  Define Move Time Matrix or use Transaction OP30 or OPJR. Figure 3.14 shows the plant-specific location group. For this example, set the Plnt (plant) as “1710,” set the Loc. Group (location group) as “A” and choose the Transport Time Matrix folder. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 91 3.3 Work Center Figure 3.14 Location Groups and Transport Time Matrix Note Move time matrix and transport time matrix are synonymous terms. In the screen that appears next, as shown in Figure 3.15, assign the standard and the minimum move times for the plant-location group combination. In the Calendar field, choose whether the move times defined are applicable every day of the week, accord- ing to the factory calendar, or according to the operating time and calendar given in the work center. When you’ve put the necessary configuration settings in place, assign the location group in the Scheduling area of the work center.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 92 3.3.6 Control Key for Operations A control key acts as a central function to control which actions a user or system can or can’t perform on a specific work center. Check the relevant boxes and make the rele- vant settings in the control key, as shown in Figure 3.16. Then, assign this control key in the Default Values area of the work center (or resource). Once you’ve assigned the work center to the material’s routing, the control key becomes an integral part of the opera- tion and acts as a control function.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.16 Control Key In a control key, it’s possible to define, among other things, whether some or all of the following functions are possible:  Scheduling  Capacity requirements planning  Inspection characteristics required for in-process (during production) inspection  Automatic GR  Scheduling for external operations The confirmation type required for a work center can also be controlled. For example, it’s possible to control whether confirmation is required or optional for a given opera- tion during the order confirmation process.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Further, whether an operation is a mile- stone confirmation can also be controlled. In a milestone confirmation, all of the pre- ceding operations are automatically confirmed as soon as the operation is confirmed as having a milestone confirmation. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 93 3.4 Routing To set up a control key for operations, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Routing  General Data  Operation Data  Define Control Key or use Transaction OP67. Note Chapter 6 will cover how to assign this control key in the Default Values area of the work center. 3.4 Routing A routing is a set of operations that the material will undergo during the entire produc- tion process at relevant work centers. For example, a raw material is transformed into a finished product due to undergoing various operations (defined in the routing) per- formed at the relevant work centers.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Most of the important parameters for routing selection are made in the order type– dependent parameters (Section 3.6), in which you incorporate controls such as routing selection as mandatory or optional requirements. The order type–dependent parame- ters also control whether routing selection is an automatic or a manual process. To set up the routing parameters, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Routing  Routing Selection  Select Automatically or use Transaction OPEB. In Figure 3.17, the selection ID specifies the selection sequence according to which the system will select the planned type, usage, and status of the routing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following list explains the first few columns:  ID This combines all of the different priorities listed in the next column, SP .  SP This lists the sequence in which the system will look for relevant routing during pro- duction order creation. In other words, it’s the priority setting for routing selection.  Task List Type This refers to the task list type that the system will consider, such as N for routing, R for rate routing, and S for reference operation set.  Plan Usage This controls whether the routing is only used for production or is available for inspection plan usage too.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The value 3 denotes that this routing will be available for all types of usages.  Description This is the description that appears after you select the relevant usage from the Plan Usage field. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 94  Status This denotes the status that the system should look for in a routing or in a reference operation set and that, if found, it should incorporate in the production order.  Description of the Status This is the description that appears after you select the relevant usage from the Description of the Status field. Figure 3.17 Automatic Routing Selection Note You can use the selection IDs during scheduling of orders (planned orders or produc- tion orders). Use Transaction OPU3, OPU4, or OPU5 to assign the relevant selection IDs to the order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: See Section 3.6.1 for how to incorporate selection IDs into production orders (Transaction OPU3). 3.5 Production Order Configuration During an SAP S/4HANA implementation, the PP consultant conducts workshops and finalizes several configuration objects, including order types and their number ranges. An order type is a unique identification and control function that enables the business process owner to quickly perform several functions, such as creating an order, auto- matically releasing an order, or scheduling an order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The decision to create and make available different order types depends on how the company wants to see data, information, and depth of planning and controls required. For example, a company might want to sort all orders by separating all of the rework © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 95 3.5 Production Order Configuration production orders from the normal production orders. This logical segregation of two different order types enables the planner to not only quickly segregate the available data in the system in the form of reports but also put in place the necessary system authorizations. Normally, companies also prefer to have production order types in direct relation to work centers. For example, in the cold-rolled steel sheets industry, if there are five different work centers—such as cold-rolled sheets uncoiling, pickling, annealing, recoiling, and packing—then it makes sense to have five different produc- tion order types to enable every work center to have clear visibility into the activities and controls involved.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, in the automotive assembly industry, the main work centers may be press shop, paint shop, and final assembly. In the textile industry, the work centers may be spinning, weaving, bleaching and dyeing, stitching, and finishing. In a pharmaceutical company, there may only be a need to create two order types—the first for bulk medicines (such as pill, capsule, and tablet manufacturing) and the second for packing bulk medicines. However, we suggest not overdoing it in this exercise: creating too many production order types can be confusing and requires lots of data entry and maintenance work.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Instead, use operations and other work center criteria to meet your reporting needs. In the following sections, we’ll discuss how to create a new production order type in dis- crete manufacturing and assign it a new number range. 3.5.1 Maintaining Order Types An order type controls the following functions directly or through additional profiles:  Internal and external number assignment  Classification system  Commitments management  Status management for the different production statuses  Settlement  Scheduling When you’re defining an order type, the system automatically assigns the relevant order category.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An order category distinguishes among various order types, not just in the production processes but also in plant maintenance (PM), quality management, and CO orders. Whenever you create a new order type for a particular application, the system automatically assigns the correct order category. Figure 3.18 shows the list of order categories available in the SAP S/4HANA system when you hover over Order category and press (F4) . A PP Production Order uses Order category 10 , whereas the Order category for a Process Order is 40 .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 96 Figure 3.18 Order Categories To create a new order type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Master Data  Order  Define Order Types or use Transaction OPJH. In Figure 3.19, notice that the system automatically assigns Order category 10 to the production order. Create Order Type “PP10” and give a short description. For the Settle- ment Profile , coordinate with the product costing team to assign the appropriate settle- ment profile to the production order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tips and Tricks To save yourself the effort of defining all the parameters in any configuration object and also to lessen the chance of errors, we suggest that you copy from one of the stan- dard objects available and then make the desired changes to the newly created object. The copy function is available in all configuration objects. Look for the Copy As button, as shown in the menu bar in Figure 3.19. For this example, copy the standard and previously available PP01 production order type to create the new PP10 production order type.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note You can also use Transaction CO82 to create a new number range group and define the interval for the production order. On the initial screen, choose Change Groups and then perform all of the steps listed in Section 3.5. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 97 3.5 Production Order Configuration Figure 3.19 Maintaining Production Order Types Scroll down in the screen shown in Figure 3.19 and choose the Number Range General button shown in Figure 3.20 to define the new number range for the newly created PP10 production order type. Figure 3.20 Number Range Creation 3.5.2 Number Ranges On the initial screen that appears, choose Create Group. On the next screen that appears, as shown in Figure 3.21, enter the new number range group. All production orders assigned to this number range group will use this number range.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, enter “Turbine” in Group and define the new number range interval as “80000001” to “84999999.” To facilitate the number range creation process, the system displays the existing number ranges available (if any) in the lower half of the screen. The newly defined number range can’t overlap with the existing number ranges. Choose Insert , and the system will enable defining a new number range interval. In this example, the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 98 newly defined number range is assigned the tag 25 , as shown on the left-hand side of Figure 3.21. This number range tag will be used to assign the number range to the newly created PP10 production order type. Next, perform the following steps: 1. Check the Turbine Manufacturing box, which represents the new number range group. 2. At the bottom of the same screen, look for Not Assigned , including the newly created PP10 production order type. Choose PP10 and then choose Select . 3.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose Element/Group . Figure 3.21 Inserting Group Screen to Enter New Number Range Interval If you successfully follow these steps in order, the final screen will look like Figure 3.22. Here, the system assigns the newly created number range group 25 to the newly cre- ated PP10 order type. Figure 3.22 Number Range Group Assigned to Order Type PP10 In Chapter 6, you’ll see that the production order for order type PP10 has the number range assigned in this step. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 99 3.6 Order Type–Dependent Plant Parameters 3.6 Order Type–Dependent Plant Parameters After you define the new order type, the next step is to define order type–dependent plant parameters. In this step, you make several settings to enable the system to control different functions during production order creation. For example, it’s possible to con- trol whether the system should automatically select the production version or provide the user with the option to select it manually in a popup that appears during production order creation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, you can assign a batch search strategy for batch-managed materials. Furthermore, it’s possible to control which information the system should update to make it a part of the order information system and logistics information sys- tem (LIS). Finally, you should coordinate with the product costing team to enable them to make relevant settings from a cost center accounting (within SAP S/4HANA Finance) perspective. To set up order type–dependent plant parameters, follow menu path SAP IMG  Produc- tion  Shop Floor Control  Master Data  Order  Define Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters or use Transaction OPL8.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Figure 3.23, notice the plant and order type combinations that are already available. For this example, select Plant 1710 and Order Type YBM1 and choose the Copy As icon to copy all settings from order type YBM1 to order type PP10. The system creates a new entry for plant 1710 and order type PP10. Figure 3.23 Available Order Type–Dependent Parameters We’ll now walk through the different tabs that are available for order type–dependent parameters. 3.6.1 Planning In the Planning tab area, shown in Figure 3.24, choose whether the system should bring up a popup window where you can manually select the Production Version or whether it should automatically assign the first available production version to the production order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the Routing area, the Selection ID is the same as that covered in Section 3.4. Choose from Selection IDs for automatic or manual routing selection (or a reference operation set) during production order creation. Also, choose whether it’s mandatory or optional for the system to have a routing (or a reference operation set) available during production order creation. Check the Check Op. Details box to enable the sys- tem to check and automatically copy the work center details in the routing. You can also copy the routing header text into the production order.

docs.text: 25 Preface A company that’s in the business of manufacturing a product that it sells to its cus- tomer goes through the rigor of using logistics, operations, supply chain management, and product lifecycle management in SAP S/4HANA. The quality management func- tionality (which we’ll refer to as QM throughout the book) in the SAP S/4HANA system plays a critical role in the company’s logistics functions to accomplish just that. QM enables the company to erect quality gates in as many of the business processes as deemed necessary to improve product quality, reduce or eliminate product defects and manufacturing waste, or simply transition toward optimizing its business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM seamlessly integrates with the company’s sales, procurement, production, ware- housing, maintenance, projects, human capital, finance, and controlling functions. In fact, it isn’t an understatement to mention that no other area so deeply and exten- sively integrates with other SAP S/4HANA system functionalities as QM does. This inte- gration, depending on the size of the organization, can possibly lead to big data that promises to provide invaluable insight to companies in making informed and timely business decisions, thereby ensuring business continuity and business growth.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: That said, it also demands that the organization’s QM team have an enormous and in- depth understanding of business processes of other SAP S/4HANA system functional- ities so that business processes can work in tandem and in complete synchronization with each other. QM in SAP S/4HANA offers wide-ranging business processes and functions to ensure that your products and their ingredients or subcomponents conform to your quality standards, whether they are regulatory, based on industry standards (e.g., the industry- sector US Food and Drug Administration [FDA], International Organization for Stan- dardization [ISO], Good Manufacturing Practices [GMP], or Federation of the German Motor Industry [VDA]), or based on internal quality standards.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The QM processes within the SAP S/4HANA system support the entire product lifecycle from conception to disposal during all parts of the logistics and supply chain. QM pro- vides a completely integrated quality management solution based on the total quality management approach, an integrative approach for continuously improving product and process quality. Total quality management includes making sure that the interac- tions of the processes are supported by an electronic data processing system. So, the QM activities that are within the scope of this book are the processes and activities put in place to ensure that the quality of end products, ingredients, and subcomponents used to produce the end product conform to quality standards.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Preface 26 Goals of This Book The first goal of this book is to provide you with a step-by-step approach to configure and implement individual business processes that integrate with QM. Each chapter lays the initial foundations in the form of configuration, and then the rest of each chap- ter shows how the configuration eventually impacts the business processes. This approach (configuration first, followed by business processes) is maintained in most parts of the book. Where it’s relevant or makes more sense to first cover business pro- cesses to help you develop a good understanding of concepts, the relevant configura- tion steps are covered at the end of the chapter instead.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In short, here’s the general approach to any topic that you’ll find in most parts of this book:  Configuration  Master data  Business processes  Reports, analyses, or optimization tools and pointers The next goal is to provide comprehensive coverage of the many features and function- alities that QM offers. However, we encourage you to evaluate each and every feature, option, and functionality to determine whether implementing it will bring clarity or improvements to your business process. You’ll need to maintain a fine balance between implementing and integrating QM in business processes to bring greater control, visi- bility, and improvement to business processes with the time, efforts, and resources involved.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Further, there are significant “hidden” or lesser-used functionalities in QM that you can integrate even when (and long after) your SAP S/4HANA system imple- mentation is complete. docs.text: 35 Chapter 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA The quality management functionality in SAP S/4HANA enables a com- pany to improve the quality of its products by continuously assessing them at any given step of the logistics and supply chain. By doing so, the company can ensure that its products conform to relevant product reg- ulations, industry standards, and/or company quality standards. Companies that want to maintain, retain, and continuously improve the quality of their products find quality management (QM) in SAP S/4HANA to be their trusted and steadfast companion in the logistics and supply chain management functions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From prequalifying potential suppliers for supplying raw and packing materials, conducting preliminary inspections before goods reach the company premises, and conducting quality tests when suppliers deliver the materials to ensuring quality inspection during and after production finds, QM integrates into all-important business processes. QM also ensures that companies can conduct another, customer-specific round of quality checks and, before dispatching goods to customers, extensively evaluate defects in their own returned products, with the aim of eliminating those defects.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM covers it all: new products developed with a stability study, continuous product and process improvements with failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and internal and external audits using audit management. Quality control ensures that companies fre- quently evaluate suppliers to maintain business relationships with them, as well as monitor critical statistical process control for products that are produced in house. The optimization in QM allows added functionality such as digital signatures that eliminate manual approval processes, manage incoming and outgoing quality certificates, and integrate Document Management System (DMS) into important business functions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM integrates completely with several key logistics and supply chain areas, including procurement, production, and sales. It can check the quality compliance of raw materials when they’re first delivered by suppliers and later during production and postproduc- tion. The QM area can also check for compliance with customers’ quality specifications before the finished goods are shipped out. QM is a wide-ranging solution that supports the company throughout the product life- cycle and along the supply chain. In particular, the QM solution offers the following benefits:  Provides a single quality management solution for all company processes, giving you a single source of truth and access to the most current quality information at any time Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: First, however, we’ll give you a good starting point: SAP’s organizational structures, which you need to understand to know how various areas of SAP work together. 1.1 Organizational Structure in SAP S/4HANA At the start of an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, one of the first and most intensive activities undertaken is the finalization of the organizational structure. This involves having intermodular and intramodular discussions and deliberations to © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 37 1.1 Organizational Structure in SAP S/4HANA ensure that the SAP S/4HANA system can both cover the legal aspects of the company’s organizational structure and attend to area-specific reporting needs. In other words, the business process owners, business analysts, and SAP consultants review the exist- ing organizational structure of the company and then simultaneously begin mapping it in the SAP S/4HANA system. A practical approach to adopt while finalizing the organizational structure in SAP S/4HANA is to ensure that the organizational structure isn’t so generic that it loses its signifi- cance and prevents the business process owner from extracting the required informa- tion from the system, nor is it so minute or detailed that it becomes cumbersome to collate and consolidate the information.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You should also keep a forward-thinking view of your organizational structure. If you foresee that you’ll need certain organizational elements in your SAP S/4HANA system in the future, for example, it’s better to have them available in the system than to add them at a later point. Although QM itself doesn’t have any of its own organizational structure to configure from an implementation perspective, you need to understand the important organiza- tional units: client, company code, plant, storage location, and warehouse number.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we’ll review the structure as it applies to QM. If QM integrates with the procurement processes, it requires an understanding of the purchasing organization and purchasing group. Similarly, if QM integrates with SAP S/4HANA Sales business processes, then you need to have a decent understanding of the sales organization, dis- tribution channel, and division, which together form the sales area. If the company has also implemented and is using embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA, then a decent understanding of the EWM structure is helpful for a QM consultant and business user.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll also discuss the importance of the organizational units and explain how they work together to accomplish the organizational, legal, and reporting requirements of the company. The organizational structure in the SAP S/4HANA system is equally applicable to all important business functions that we cover in the entire book. Figure 1.1 shows the cli- ent as the highest level of the organizational structure in the SAP S/4HANA system. The profitability analysis of the company is performed at the controlling area level, and the cost center and profit center accountings are performed at that level as well.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A company can consist of several legal entities, each including separate, individual financial statements that must be prepared at the end of the financial year. This is reflected as a separate company code for each legal entity. The valuation area represents the level at which the company values its material stock consistently. It’s part of the logistics area of the SAP S/4HANA system. A one-to-one relationship exists between the valuation area and the plant. For example, a material at one plant may have a different standard price than at another plant, where its price control may be a moving average.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 39 1.1 Organizational Structure in SAP S/4HANA 1.1.1 Client A client represents the highest element of the SAP S/4HANA system’s organizational structure. Often, the client represents a company or group of companies, within which there are several independent company units. An SAP S/4HANA system can contain several clients in logical units. The additional organizational elements and the master and transaction data are created and managed within a client. From the SAP S/4HANA system’s landscape perspective, you normally have at least three clients (systems): DEV (development), QAS (quality assurance system), and PRD (production).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The actual configuration of the SAP S/4HANA system takes place in the DEV system and is then transported to the QAS system for testing and training. The final configuration eventually moves to PRD, which is the final live system in which the business process owners of the company make real-time, live entries. 1.1.2 Company Code The company code is the level below the client in the SAP S/4HANA system, and it reflects the level at which the company legally reports income statements and balance sheets. It’s an organizational element (unit) of the financial accounting area.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can have a separate company code for each line of business—for example, textiles and chemicals—so long as the two are legally separate entities. Similarly, separate company codes can exist if the company has operations in foreign countries. 1.1.3 Plant A plant is an organizational unit in the logistics area. You can classify a plant from the point of view of production, procurement, maintenance, warehouse, and planning. The plant can be, for example, a manufacturing site, a head office, or a distribution center within a company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It organizes the tasks for logistics, and it can be a physical produc- tion site or the logical grouping of several sites in which materials are produced or goods and services are provided. 1.1.4 Storage Location A storage location is a physical or virtual storage site for materials. Examples of physi- cal storage locations include raw material store, components store, returned goods store, finished goods store, and so on, whereas a virtual storage location can be self- defined and may be a scrapyard, a production shop floor in which semifinished goods are temporarily stored, and so on.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 40 1.1.5 Warehouse Number A warehouse complex is represented in the SAP S/4HANA system as a warehouse num- ber, and all the warehouse processes, such as picking and putaway, are executed using this warehouse number. The warehouse number doesn’t have an address but has a short descriptive text. This is unlike a storage location, which holds an address. Within the SAP S/4HANA system, assignment of a warehouse number to a plant and storage location combination identifies which storage location is controlled by the warehouse management system (WMS). 1.2 Quality Management in the SAP Landscape QM offers a wide range of functions and business processes that fully integrate with SAP Product Lifecycle Management (SAP PLM) and focuses on ensuring and managing the quality of products and assets.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Accordingly, QM is an integral part of the SAP PLM solution map under the main process product development and collaboration (see Table 1.1). It includes the prevention of quality-related problems and offers continuous process improvement abilities through collaboration and sustained quality control. So, in the broader sense, QM focuses on the entirety of all QM-relevant processes for a product (quality planning, quality certificate, quality notification, quality control, test equipment management, and stability study).
