docs.text: 41 1.3 Business Processes in Quality Management Hardly any business process owner works in an SAP S/4HANA system without coordi- nating and collaborating with multiple areas. These areas reflect different business functions, processes, or needs of the company. Depending on the scope of your QM activities or QM implementation in your organization, you’ll probably use other sup- porting areas, including the following:  Logistics and supply chain management To cover all the functional areas available in logistics, for example, SAP S/4HANA Sales, materials management (MM), inventory management, embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA, production planning (PP), plant maintenance (PM), logistics execu- tion, and so on.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A significant portion of this book is devoted to showing QM integra- tion with the PP, MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, embedded EWM, and PM areas.  Financial accounting and controlling To perform activities within financial accounting and controlling, such as analyzing quality cost, setting up labor rates and overhead rates, and so on.  Classification system To set up quality catalogs for recording results, for multiple specification, and for using within batch management (see Chapter 9).  Engineering change management To control the change process for quality documents, inspection plans, and so on (see Chapter 13).  Document Management System (DMS) To store quality documents, such as manuals, procedures, or quality certificates.  Audit management To use the audit processes, including audit plans, audit questionnaires, and so on (see Chapter 14).  Equipment serialization To conduct quality tests on calibration equipment that is managed using serial numbers (see Chapter 7). 1.3 Business Processes in Quality Management We’ll now discuss the four important pillars of QM that are vital to a company’s contin- ued business success and the business processes they cover:  Quality engineering  Quality assurance and control  Quality improvement  Product change management Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 42 1.3.1 Quality Engineering Simply put, quality engineering ensures that quality standards are incorporated into and ingrained in every important business process. This process helps organizations eliminate defects, improve product quality, reduce customer complaints, and more by designing (that’s engineering here!) an excellent quality product. It’s important to have the correct quality planning strategies, processes, tools, and mechanisms in place during the early stages of product design and development.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Qual- ity engineering provides the functions and tools to incorporate these quality aspects throughout the entire product development process, which is why it plays such a fun- damental role during new product development and introduction (NPDI). The goal of quality engineering is to promote “quality by design” rather than “quality by test.” The quality engineering process includes closed-loop inspection planning. A closed- loop inspection plan is an integrated inspection planning process for goods receipt inspection and inspection during production.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s an iterative process in which changes can be initiated from any activity in the loop, and it provides functions and features for understanding the effect of the change on the other objects (the closed loop). Closed- loop inspection planning enables you to perform FMEA, set up a control plan, and set up the inspection planning details. This process includes efficient supplier manage- ment, maintenance of quality-related documents, and recipe management when required. Quality engineering is focused on incorporating quality into the entire product devel- opment process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The quality engineering business processes ensure that the quality of your products is correct from product idea through product delivery and into service at the customer’s site. The quality engineering process often starts with the setup of a project, which can include defined deliverables, quality gates, and stability studies. After these initial stages, you continue quality engineering by closed-loop inspection planning. Quality engineering can have a very high impact on other logistics supply chain business pro- cesses within an organization because quality is crucial for most industries, is part of the integrated value chain, and has a strong influence on costs.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Two related concepts that are important to quality engineering are FMEA and control plans; these both play a role in the closed-loop inspection planning process. These are relatively new concepts, and their steps fulfill important requirements for several industries. However, they aren’t required to perform quality engineering activities or to set up an inspection planning process or complaints processes. You can find more information about FMEA in Chapter 16. The quality engineering process starts with closed-loop inspection planning.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 43 1.3 Business Processes in Quality Management 1. Define the development project Efficient project management is one of the cornerstones of successful product development. Quality management during product development starts with defin- ing the deliverables and quality gates, which includes inspection planning, effi- ciently managing suppliers, and setting up quality-related documents. In several industries (mainly process industries), this process includes the performance of sta- bility studies. 2. Manage the quality master data and inspection plans In general, quality planning consists of all the activities required to ensure the prod- uct’s quality and provides the basis for effective quality assurance and control.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s a continuous iterative process managed by multiple departments (e.g., procurement, production, and quality engineering) and requiring a high degree of collaboration. 3. Plan and execute stability studies Stability studies give you a means of testing and evaluating products during various stages of the product lifecycle so you can determine how products or product batches will hold up under controlled environmental conditions over predefined periods of time. For example, you can use a stability study to investigate a product’s shelf life based on conditions such as temperature, moisture, atmospheric pressure, and brightness.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Stability studies during product development are also often used to determine the ideal product composition and/or the most suitable product packag- ing. They allow you to meet legal requirements, such as GMP. In addition to being suitable for use in process industries (e.g., chemicals, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and foods), stability studies can be conducted in specific areas of discrete manufac- turing (e.g., to test the stability of paints in the automotive supplier industry). 4. Maintain a quality manual Companies use the quality management system as a tool for analyzing and improv- ing their business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Various industry standards also require companies to establish and maintain a process-oriented quality manual. You can also include other quality management documentation—standard operating procedures, qual- ity certificates, and quality manuals—and store that documentation with DMS. After quality engineering, the next logical QM activity is quality assurance and control, which enables you to maintain and improve the attained level of product quality. Qual- ity assurance and control involves inspections at all stages of a product’s lifecycle, its continuous monitoring, and quick intervention to deal with unexpected events. 1.3.2 Quality Assurance and Control After your quality processes are in place, you need to maintain and improve the attained level of quality.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Quality control involves inspections at all stages, continuous monitoring, and intervening quickly to deal with unexpected events. Quality assur- ance and control checks can be performed during any step within the logistics value Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 44 chain with the goal of ensuring that the quality of a product conforms to the necessary quality standards. The quality assurance and control business processes describe general logistics quality assurance activities, such as requesting and checking quality certificates from suppliers and/or suppliers at the time of goods receipt of a purchase order. On goods receipt at a storage location (e.g., a warehouse), the incoming certificate is checked and electroni- cally stored as part of quality assurance.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Another quality assurance activity—and the main activity that QM supports—is the set up and performance of quality inspections as part of the logistics supply chain. The quality inspection process includes the setup of the master data relevant for quality inspection, quality planning, the quality trigger (an event, e.g., a goods receipt, goods issue, or customer complaint), the sample infor- mation, the inspection itself, the recording of the results, and the validation of the results, followed by a usage decision and any follow-up activities.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Often, batch manage- ment is used to provide full traceability of the used ingredients or components. Basically, all the quality inspection process steps can be divided into four distinct phases: the trigger, the request for an inspection, the inspection itself, and any follow- up activities, as shown in Figure 1.3. Figure 1.3 Quality Inspection Process Steps Let’s also briefly consider other supplementary areas often conducted with QM. The following supplementary QM functions are often covered under the quality assurance and quality control process:  Test equipment interfacing A standardized interface for connecting measuring subsystems and for external control of inspection operations on the shop-floor level.  Statistical process control The application of statistical techniques to control a process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This is used inter- changeably with statistical quality control. Six Sigma approaches are supported to analyze measured values and nonconformance data, such as the use of various qual- ity control charts, Western Electric rules, capability indicators, Pareto analysis, trend analysis, and exception analysis. In addition, SAP Manufacturing Integration and What triggers an inspection? • Unexpected event • Planned event • Analytical event What and how much is inspected? • Inspection lot and instruction • Sample drawing instruction What are the results of the inspection? • Result recording • Defects recording What should happen to the goods? • Usage decision Trigger Request for inspection Inspection Decision © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 45 1.3 Business Processes in Quality Management Intelligence (SAP MII) can be used as a frontend tool to visualize quality data from QM and execute statistical process control.  Laboratory information management system (LIMS) Facilitates the testing of samples that routinely pass through an analytical lab. The trend of shifting from isolated data islands to global information is followed due to its tight integration into supply chain components, which offers functions for inventory control and batch tracking, as well as problem handling and management of corrective action and preventive action.  GAAP compliance (according to ISO 9000) Good Clinical Practice/Good Laboratory Practice/Good Manufacturing Practice (GCP/GLP/GMP) include guidelines for enterprises that are regulated by the FDA.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP S/4HANA provides all the functions necessary to fulfill such requirements. For example, it supports FDA document control, digital signature, audit trial, batch traceability, and electronic batch records. SAP’s development and service organiza- tions are certified according to ISO 9000. While ISO 9000 is a family of ISO stan- dards that provide a general framework for quality management standards, ISO 9001 is a subgroup of the ISO 9000 family that lays out the requirements for meet- ing quality management standards as discussed later in Table 1.2 in this chapter.  Quality costs Includes the cost associated with inspecting a product to ensure that it meets the internal or external customer’s needs and requirements.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It includes the costs associ- ated with providing poor quality products or services. Once you’ve established your quality processes and can maintain them, it’s time to take them to the next level with quality improvement. 1.3.3 Quality Improvement Quality improvement records quality problems and includes problem-solving by sys- tematically determining their cause, solution, follow-up, and actions. The quality noti- fication process is available to document problems of any type for this purpose— especially problems related to poor quality of a product, such as processing complaints against suppliers and complaints from customers.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It can also be used to process an internal company problem relating to processes and products and for handling posi- tive events, such as proposals for improvement. The notification is the document used to capture these events. Let’s walk through the process: 1. Record problems Via the notification, you can record and process different types of problems, such as those resulting from poor-quality goods or services received from a supplier or deliv- ered to a customer. During notification processing and inspection processing, you can be alerted about similar or related problems, helping you prevent a repetition.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 46 2. Manage and coordinate problem notifications The quality coordinator defines the problem details, the individual defects, the defect causes, and a priority (often including response times), and then dispatches the notification to suitable experts by assigning them the follow-up tasks and activ- ities. 3. Analyze individual problems and causes The quality coordinator generally requires the assistance of a technical specialist to weigh in on the product’s defects. The expert investigates the problem, detects the causes, suggests a solution, and records these findings in the notification to enable standardization and reporting.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When set up, the expert can use the solution data- base, which can assist in finding an appropriate solution based on the symptoms of the problem. 4. Assign corrective and preventive actions After finalizing the defects and their causes, the technical specialist will typically consult the people responsible for the defect causes to cooperate with them in defin- ing corrective actions and preventive actions and assigning the partners responsible for processing these tasks. 5. Carry out corrective and preventive actions Within the notification worklist, you can see the outstanding corrective actions and preventive actions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Corrective tasks must be processed in a series of traceable steps. For example, the automotive industry uses the Eight Disciplines of Problem-Solving (8D) process, in which all eight steps are required to solve a problem and must be documented. 6. Monitor problems and actions After processing and completing all the outstanding corrective actions and preven- tive actions, and once the solution has been approved by the problem initiator, com- munication to other interested parties may be required, after which the notification can be considered as completed.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Quality managers can use the quality management information system (QMIS) to per- form the following QM analytics:  Compare the frequency of similar notifications and defects for different reference objects (e.g., with reference to different materials, suppliers, or customers) to infer the main problem sources.  Analyze the recorded defects, and monitor the correction of these problems by checking that the corrective actions and preventive actions have been followed up within the established time frames.  Evaluate the problem data.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can, for example, perform a Pareto analysis of the most frequent defect types and defect causes, or perform a Pareto analysis of the materials and business partners most frequently affected by problems to find the main problems and starting points for improvements. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 47 1.3 Business Processes in Quality Management  Perform exception analyses, which identify apparent exceptional situations related to the problem and thereby provide impetuses for defect prevention and improve- ment tasks. Apart from using the QMIS, you can use additional reporting tools, such as SAP Busi- ness Warehouse (SAP BW), SAP BusinessObjects Business Intelligence (SAP Business- Objects BI), or both, with the activation of QM-specific content. Notification data can be analyzed with SAP BusinessObjects BI, in which advanced evaluation tools are available to quality managers.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Quality improvement is the last area within the scope of product quality management. We’ll continue with product change management within engi- neering change management. 1.3.4 Product Change Management Product change management represents the definition and efficient management of engineering changes to ensure that your product data is up-to-date (i.e., representing the latest changes) and that product quality in all phases of the product lifecycle is met. Product change management is addressed by SAP PLM’s engineering change manage- ment, available within the SAP system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It includes all types of changes (e.g., form, fit, and function) with processes and procedures that manage how changes are proposed, reviewed, approved, and incorporated into a product and its associated data items. This engineering change management process provides the means to proactively manage all product changes before product information is handed over to supply chain opera- tions (manufacturing, procurement, service/maintenance, recalls, etc.), along with workflows and full visibility of the impact when changes are initiated from supply chain operations.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Companies can achieve the following business goals and objectives by implementing engineering change management:  Increases customer satisfaction, service, and delivery with last-minute changes by reducing product errors, constantly improving product quality, and capturing prod- uct changes easily and quickly.  Satisfies the requirement to document and monitor the change process by includ- ing the change history of the affected object with a before and after status to ensure consistency of products.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It includes the ability to specify that changes are effective only under defined conditions and the ability to group changes that belong together.  Integrates with the logistics value chain, where changes can automatically be per- formed for a sales order, a process order, material requirements planning (MRP) set- tings, or product details based on a release key.  Ensures that all people affected by the changes—including data consumers—are involved in the change process. The change process can be flexibly configured to cater to specific business requirements, which can optionally use workflow-driven tasks.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 48  Increases transparency and accountability for the secure and reproducible change process for the package of all objects affected by the change, which provides a single source of truth. Parallel processing of changes is possible due to optimal use of change packages.  Reduces operating costs and increases efficiency by reducing product returns, reducing rework required on production orders, and providing seamless, rule-based transfer of product structure changes to operative production orders via order change management.  Reduces time to volume due to the phased release of the engineering change order to subsequent areas.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Let’s now review the role of QM in inbound and outbound logistics and supply chain management, as well as how it integrates with these areas. 1.4 Integration with Other Areas The importance of building quality checks and material inspections into every stage of the supply chain can’t be overemphasized. Besides saving time and money in the short term, integrating QM into critical processes can deliver greater business benefits well into the future. Figure 1.4 represents a generalized logistic value chain: the diamonds represent quality gates that you can implement and through which the product must pass in the logistics and supply chain processes before it moves on to the next step.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 49 1.4 Integration with Other Areas In the following sections, we’ll briefly review some of the business processes in which QM integrates with logistics areas. 1.4.1 Materials Management The QM integration with materials management (MM) attends to quality inspections of all procured materials. Inspections can be triggered even before goods are delivered, which allows a company’s representatives to visit suppliers to check the quality of the goods they produce. The scope and complexities of MM are very large, so we restrict ourselves to covering either the integration points of QM with MM or where business processes in MM directly impact QM.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following subfunctions are heavily integrated with QM:  Procurement  Inventory management For business processes in the procurement area, you’ll need MM’s organizational struc- ture, such as the purchasing organization and purchasing group. For inventory man- agement business processes, you’ll need the plant and storage location, which we covered previously. The following are the organizational units that you need to ensure are available in the system so that your procurement processes run in the system and with which you can integrate QM:  Purchasing organization A purchasing organization can be a logical or actual division of a company’s pur- chasing functions and is responsible for managing and reporting procurement func- tions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, a purchasing organization can be a local or imports business.  Purchasing group A purchasing group is a person or group of persons responsible for the procurement of group of materials or services. Examples of purchase groups are raw materials, chemicals, maintenance spares, or consumables. When you create a purchasing group, it’s important to ensure that it isn’t created with a person’s name because that person’s role or area of responsibility may change. 1.4.2 Production Planning When integrated with production planning (PP), QM adds two additional types of qual- ity inspections: in-process and finished goods.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: During the production process, an in- process inspection ascertains the quality of goods in production. In this situation, the user performs the QM results recording, defects recording, and usage decision steps before releasing the material to the next stage of production. It’s also possible to embed quality controls in the production process so that the next step of a production Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 50 process only begins after the quality results and usage decision from the previous step are recorded in the system. Further, it’s also possible to incorporate quality inspection processes as soon as compo- nents or materials required in the production processes are issued out. For finished goods, the user performs the three quality steps before the stock is released for sale or consumption. In summary, three types of quality inspections are possible in a produc- tion process—goods issue, in-process, and goods receipt inspection—and in all three manufacturing types: discrete, process, and repetitive.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The quality management processes work well even when a company has implemented the embedded production planning and detailed scheduling (PP-DS) functionality of PP in SAP S/4HANA. 1.4.3 Sales If the customer requires additional quality checks before goods can be dispatched, QM can handle them once it’s integrated with SAP S/4HANA Sales. When goods are issued against a sales order, the SAP S/4HANA system creates an automatic inspection lot that must first be checked for compliance with the customer’s quality specifications.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM can also trigger an inspection when a customer returns defective goods. The business processes in SAP S/4HANA Sales are generally the starting point in the entire chain of business events. These are the organizational units of SAP S/4HANA Sales:  Sales organization A sales organization can be a logical or actual division of a company’s sales functions and is responsible for managing and reporting sales functions. For example, a sales organization can be a local or exports business.  Distribution channel A distribution channel is the logical or actual way or channel through which the company distributes or sells its products.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Examples of distribution channels include retail, wholesale, institutional, government, or large corporate clients.  Division A division is the actual or logical group of a company’s products for which it wants to see its sales results or profits. Divisions can be cars, spare parts, or services for the automobile industry, or medicines, cosmetics, or consumer products for an herbal pharmaceutical company. 1.4.4 Plant Maintenance If plant maintenance (PM) is used for routine, preventive, or predictive plant mainte- nance, companies should perform additional quality checks on equipment to ensure © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 51 1.4 Integration with Other Areas that it adheres to minimal maintenance criteria. They can do so by integrating QM with PM. It’s also possible to use QM to map inspection scenarios into other business processes, including the following:  Plant-to-plant inspections, in which goods transferred among various plants or dis- tribution centers within the company go through quality checks to ensure that there are no damages during transportation  Physical sample inspections, in which a company’s or competitor’s sample is evalu- ated to help in important decisions, such as whether to buy the material from a new supplier or change product specifications to match those of competitors  Manual inspections in such situations as creating inspection lots for stored raw materials or finished goods or after natural or manmade disasters  Inspections for stability studies performed on products under development to ensure that they meet certain physical or chemical specifications  Custom inspections when the standard inspections in QM fail to meet particular business needs, such as integration with third-party quality management tools or inspection results from laboratory equipment 1.4.5 Embedded Extended Warehouse Management Embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA has introduced significant improvements in the entire logistics and supply chain in general and QM in particular.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The need to create and replicate embedded EWM master data, such as prod- uct master or location, is eliminated in SAP S/4HANA, making it faster and smoother to run embedded EWM integrated business processes. There is, however, still a need to set up queued remote function calls (qRFCs) in SAP S/4HANA for embedded EWM so that the transactional data communicates between SAP S/4HANA and embedded EWM. Almost all embedded EWM integrated business processes are available in embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA, and the ones that aren’t available yet are slated to be available in future releases. 1.4.6 ISO 9001 Certification Process and SAP S/4HANA Table 1.2 shows the core elements of the ISO 9001 standard and the options for imple- menting them using the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, only a few essential standard requirements are dealt with because a complete analysis of the standard with all its requirements would go far beyond the scope of this table. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 52 Standard ISO 9001 Requirement Implementation Option in SAP S/4HANA QM system : Processes must be identified and defined. The system must be docu- mented, and documents and records must be controlled. You’ve identified and defined the processes through the introduction of the SAP S/4HANA system and the selection of functionalities, especially QM. The documentation of the implementation, which is required anyway, can also be used for the documentation of your QM system, or it can be par- tially referred to for this reason.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Documentation require- ments : The documentation of the management system must adhere to certain requirements. Documents and records must be con- trolled. The entire SAP S/4HANA system is designed in such a way that this requirement is fulfilled. Each creation and modifica- tion of documents and records (as long as they are processed through the SAP system) is recorded with user name, date, and time. This means that relevant proof is always available. The release after inspection is implemented via a status con- cept, and the appropriate personnel are defined through the authorization concept and the responsibility for certain pro- cesses.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Special authorizations are to be implemented using a digital signature. DMS is particularly suitable for implement- ing this standard requirement. Management responsibility : Responsibility and authority must be specified and docu- mented, resources must be provided, and QM evaluation must be performed. The implementation of the SAP S/4HANA system, the use of the required modules, the responsibilities for the mapped processes, and the authorization concept ensure that numer- ous requirements are met directly. The SAP S/4HANA infor- mation systems provide access to nearly all facts you require for the QM evaluation.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Capability, consciousness, and training : The training require- ment must be identified, nec- essary qualifications must be attained, and records on the training status must be maintained. You can meet the requirement to record the training status by using the human resources (HR) functionality. There you can manage the corresponding information for each employee. Evaluating the contractual requirements with regard to the product (contract check- ing and managing changes) : Checking the requirements and the capability to meet them.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This element is supported by the SAP S/4HANA system in dif- ferent areas. You can manage contracts using DMS. The material master data enables you to review a part of the requirements. You can use PP and standalone SAP EWM and embedded EWM to check the capacity. The engineering change management with the change master record (date, processor, etc.) allows you to manage contract changes, and the entire system records all management data. In addition, you can create or supplement records with comment fields in different transactions and by using the notification tool.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 53 1.4 Integration with Other Areas Development (design control): Development and phase planning; defining organiza- tional and technical inter- faces; establishing and documenting development entries; verifying, document- ing, and validating results; and documenting changes. These requirements can for the most part be covered by existing areas. You can plan a development project and its phases with the project system (PS) functionality. SAP PLM ensures integration into the supply chain and QM. You’ll find the organizational and technical interfaces at different points in the SAP S/4HANA system, and you must define and describe them there.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Important interfaces for a development and production company include purchasing (MM) and pro- duction (PP). The procurement specifications are all available in the sys- tem (e.g., material master with individual purchase order texts, purchasing info record, supplier info record, quality info record, etc.), and you can refer to them when ordering, when goods are received, or during incoming goods inspec- tion. For verification, precisely plannable inspections are available in QM. Controlling production and services (process control) : Pro- duction, assembly, and ser- vice processes must be planned and executed under controlled conditions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Routings provides the best options for planning the produc- tion and assembly processes or services. You can specify the type of production and service, including the relevant pro- duction resources and tools or operating supplies. You can plan the maintenance of your products and production facili- ties with customer services and PM for preventive mainte- nance. Identification and traceability (and inspection status) : The product must be clearly iden- tified during production; that is, the inspection status of a product must be indicated everywhere.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP S/4HANA is quite flexible with regard to product identifi- cation and can easily meet the standard requirements. In each phase, you can print out the corresponding papers for identification and attach them to the goods, for example, the receipt of goods certificate for the inbound delivery, the pro- duction order for production, or the delivery note and the test certificate for the outbound delivery. It’s possible to print out labels with a barcode, if required. Identification and traceability (and inspection status) : The product must be clearly iden- tified during production; that is, the inspection status of a product must be indicated everywhere.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP S/4HANA is quite flexible with regard to product identifi- cation and can easily meet the standard requirements. In each phase, you can print out the corresponding papers for identification and attach them to the goods, for example, the receipt of goods certificate for the inbound delivery, the pro- duction order for production, or the delivery note and the test certificate for the outbound delivery. It’s possible to print out labels with a barcode, if required. Standard ISO 9001 Requirement Implementation Option in SAP S/4HANA Table 1.2 How SAP S/4HANA Supports the ISO 9001 Certification (Cont.) Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 54 SAP S/4HANA also supports the management of physical samples and batches. Serial number management enables you to trace individual products, if necessary. The status of the products is documented in the system, for instance, via confirmation messages for certain operations. If required, you can also print out work papers or labels to indicate the inspection status. The system can be configured so that no product can be dis- patched without having completed the required inspections and having documented them.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Property of the customer (products provided) : The prop- erty of the customer must be identified, verified, and pro- tected. You can carry out verification with SAP S/4HANA, for instance, via goods receipt inspection. Product maintenance (stor- age, etc.) : Suitable methods and processes for identifica- tion, handling, packing, stor- age, protection, and dispatch must be adopted. You can adjust your system to these standard requirements with MM, embedded EWM, and SAP S/4HANA Sales. For instance, for methods and processes that have to be adhered to at certain stages of the production process or with regard to product maintenance, you can include detailed descrip- tions as long texts at any time in routings and inspection plans.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Control of monitoring and test equipment (test equip- ment monitoring): Test equipment, provided it’s nec- essary for the fulfillment of quality requirements, must be released and calibrated or verified at regular intervals. Records must be kept on the calibration and verification results. The combined possibilities of the PM and QM areas of SAP S/4HANA enable complete test equipment monitoring. This test equipment monitoring contains the master data for all test equipment, the status (locked, free, etc.), the manage- ment (who has which item of test equipment where), and the calibration monitoring, which ensures that each item of test equipment subject to monitoring is regularly recali- brated on the basis of a maintenance plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As usual, all data on test equipment monitoring is stored in the system data- base and is available for information or further evaluation. It’s also possible to integrate a subsystem that may already exist for test equipment monitoring, which communicates with the SAP S/4HANA system through a dedicated interface. docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 55 1.5 Summary 1.5 Summary This chapter began with covering what QM is and the importance of QM integration with logistics and areas of supply chain management. The QM master data objects are important during processes relevant for ensuring product quality. We continued with the business processes within QM, starting with quality engineering. Then, we also quickly showed you how QM relates to the rest of the SAP S/4HANA landscape, as it’s important to understand the enterprise structure of various SAP S/4HANA systems that you’ll use throughout the book.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Setting up the correct and complete enterprise struc- ture is one of the key success factors for ensuring effective reporting that eventually helps in making important and strategic business decisions. The chapter also covered how SAP S/4HANA supports the ISO 9001 certification process. In the next chapter, we begin our journey in the QM area with a look at quality plan- ning. Internal audit: An audit pro- gram must be planned— criteria, scope, frequency, and methods must be defined— and records must be main- tained.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Audit management is directly supported by the SAP S/4HANA system. You can also use the quality notification to document and trace audits. Improvements (corrective and preventive action): Corrective measures must evaluate errors, including customer complaints. You’ll find the direct implementation of these requirements in the QM and PP areas in particu- lar. You can create, trace, and determine causes, prevent recurring errors, initiate mea- sures, record results, and evaluate measures. Preventive measures must determine possible errors and causes, prevent the occurrence of errors, initiate actions, record results, and evaluate actions; corrective and preven- tive actions work directly through error recording for the inspection results and the use decision.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can use your own action catalogs or initiate individual measures or actions using free texts and quality notifications, and you can trace and monitor these over time. All information and quality records are available from in-process and final inspec- tions involving production. You can record customer com- plaints, initiate corresponding actions, and further trace them via the quality notification. The SAP S/4HANA system can provide information at any time on all actions, steps, and their processing status, as well as provide information for a QM evaluation.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Standard ISO 9001 Requirement Implementation Option in SAP S/4HANA Table 1.2 How SAP S/4HANA Supports the ISO 9001 Certification (Cont.) Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 57 Chapter 2 Quality Planning As with any SAP area, the success (and failure) of an SAP S/4HANA imple- mentation project depends heavily on complete, correct, and compre- hensive master data maintenance. Quality planning ensures that the relevant master data is in place to enable you to perform quality inspec- tion. The quality planning area uses a particularly large amount of cross-functionality master data from materials management (MM), production planning (PP), SAP S/4HANA Sales, and other logistics areas. The quality planning process entails setting up not just the mas- ter data in quality management (QM) but also the master data of other SAP S/4HANA areas that integrate with QM.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, while we cover QM master data in detail, we also provide a brief overview of master data of other areas for comprehension and understanding only. Before accessing this data, it’s highly recommended that you dis- cuss how you’ll use the data of these areas with the persons responsible for them. These discussions usually result in new ideas for system use and highlight other potential synergies in the area of QM integration. It’s also important to understand how the sequence of master data maintenance generally helps in maintaining consistency in predecessor-successor relationships.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we follow the same sequence of important QM master data creation. Note Throughout this book, we’ll either be covering the relevant master data or specific master data settings that you’ll need to run the relevant business processes. At the same time, we’ll be referring to the content of this chapter so that you ensure the QM master data checklist is in place to run the relevant business processes. Table 2.1 provides an initial overview of the relevant master data. We’ll explain the most important points for QM in detail in this chapter.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because QM heavily integrates with other SAP S/4HANA areas such as MM, embedded extended warehouse manage- ment (EWM), plant maintenance (PM), or PP, it’s highly recommended to closely work with consultants and business users of these areas to ensure complete and correct availability of master data. Where possible or required, specific master data of another SAP S/4HANA area that has direct implications on QM is discussed in this chapter—and even throughout the book. docs.text: 59 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Let’s now delve into discussing and maintaining the important master data of Table 2.1. 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master When a company decides to implement QM to integrate its business processes with logistics and the supply chain and to bring about improvements to business processes, one of the very first master data maintenance tasks required is maintaining the Quality management view of the material master. The material master record in the SAP system is a complex and central entity, the pur- pose of which is to control business and logistical processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For the sake of clarity and visibility, the system divides the material master record into different views. Maintain- ing master data is a combined and collective responsibility of various departments or persons. There is also the Quality management view (see Figure 2.1) of the material master. If this view of the material isn’t available initially, the person responsible for the material master record can add it later at any time. This has no effect on any part of the logistics process (e.g., inventory management, procurement, production).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The functions for inspection-lot creation, stock posting, and—in particular—QM procure- ment control are activated later, when the Quality management view is maintained further. You set up an inspection type in the Quality management view of the material master, which acts as a control function for all subsequent activities. An inspection type is the basic identifier for the different types of inspections available in the SAP system. To add an inspection type to a material master, use Transaction MM02 or follow menu path SAP  Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Material  Change  Immediately .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the screen that appears, enter Material “RM17” and Plant “1710”, and then click Quality Management to go to the Quality management view, as shown in Figure 2.1. Material specification QM/MM Material master record Quality info record: procure- ment QM/MM Procurement Quality info record: sales QM/SAP S/4HANA Sales Sales General Master Data Area(s) Use in QM Table 2.1 Master Data of QM and Its Use in Other Logistics Areas (Cont.) docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 60 Figure 2.1 Quality Management View of Material Master Tips and Tricks If the Quality management view hasn’t been previously maintained, use Transaction MM01 to create the Quality management view of the material master first. Figure 2.1 shows the Quality management view of material RM17 for plant 1710, which includes the following important fields:  QM Material Auth. (authorization) helps to control who is authorized to perform inspection-related tasks on this material. This field also controls the digital signature in SAP, which is discussed in Chapter 3.  GR Processing Time is the average number of working days it takes it to process an inspection lot.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system uses this information during material requirements planning (MRP) to take the inspection duration into account while planning pro- curement, production, or availability of a material.  A Catalog Profile consists of defects and defect locations and is available during quality notification creation (see Chapter 12 for more details).  Material Status is the control function that allows or disallows the functions or busi- ness processes possible for this material. For example, a control function such as a material may be blocked from procurement, or the material may be obsolete.  Inspection Interval denotes the frequency with which a batch-managed material under- goes recurring (repeat) inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 61 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master The control functions in the Procurement Data area are covered in Chapter 4. Click on the Insp. Setup button in Figure 2.1 to go to Figure 2.2, which shows the initial screen of Inspection Setup Data . Because no inspection type existed when you first clicked on the Insp. Setup button, you’ll find a blank screen. You can incorporate or set up a new inspection type with the Inspection Types button shown in Figure 2.2. Inspection type 01 is relevant for the quality inspection of raw material (or other procured materials) on goods receipt against a purchase order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s important to note that assignment of an inspection type to a material is plant-specific. You can assign more than one inspection type to a material. For example, a batch-man- aged finished good with a shelf-life expiration date is inspected on its production com- pletion (known as goods receipt inspection against production order), but then the same finished good also undergoes periodic inspection if it remains unsold and its batch’s shelf life is about to expire (known as recurring inspection). Figure 2.2 Inspection Setup Data Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 62 Consider another example: the company’s business process requires inspection of a raw material at the supplier’s premises for compliance with important quality parameters prior to its delivery into the company’s warehouse (known as source inspection). The same raw material will again go through another round of quality inspection when the goods reach the company’s warehouse (known as goods receipt inspection against the purchase order). This requires activation of two different inspection types.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The first inspection type is for inspection at the supplier premises, and the second inspection type is for inspection at the company’s premises. When you want to activate a specific inspection type, you need to ensure that the Active checkbox is selected. Due to changes in the business process, if a particular inspection type is no longer needed, simply dese- lecting the Active checkbox deactivates it. This is the easiest way to deactivate an inspec- tion type at any time. You can also delete the entire inspection type, if needed.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Based on your business needs and at any point in time, you can add a new inspection type or make changes to control indicators of an already existing inspection type in Inspection Setup . Warning On deactivating or deleting an inspection type, you first have to ensure that there is no quality stock. Now, click Insp. type det. (inspection type details; the right button [the magnifying glass]) to view the details of the fields and other options available for inspection type 01. Table 2.2 explains some of the important fields of Figure 2.2.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Control Indicator Effects Post to Insp. Stock Posts a goods movement to the inspection stock for the material. Only in the QM area, within the scope of the usage decision, can you release anything out of quality inspection stock. In an exceptional case, the movement type itself enables the system to determine whether to post the quantity to inspection stock. Insp. with Mat Spec. With this indicator set, you can use a material specifica- tion to carry out an inspection. An inspection that uses a material specification can be in addition to, or even replace, an inspection that uses a routing or a master rec- ipe.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You need to completely maintain a material specifica- tion for the material to carry out an inspection. Refer to Section 2.12 on how to set up a material specification. Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 63 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Insp. with Task List With this indicator set, the system requires a task list for an inspection with the inspection lot. The decision on whether a routing or a master recipe is required is made during inspection data maintenance in the material mas- ter record. The system can only determine the sample size after assignment of the task list to the inspection lot. In Chapter 3, you’ll see that when the system is unable to find and assign a task list to an inspection lot, it’s unable to calculate the sample size.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Insp. by Configuration If this indicator is set, the system takes configurations from the sales order or production order into account in inspection-lot creation. Automatic Assignment The system tries to automatically assign a routing, an inspection plan, or a material specification to the inspec- tion lot. Inspect Charcs If you want characteristic-based results recording, you have to use a routing, an inspection plan, or a material specification for the inspection. Characteristic-based results recording is a prerequisite for characteristic-based dynamic modification.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can select a dynamic modifi- cation level in an inspection plan. Smpl. Procedure A procedure to determine the size of the sample in an inspection. The sampling procedure also defines the valu- ation type used for results recording (attributive, variable, manual, etc.). This field is of significance only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing, master recipe, or material specifica- tion. If you enter a sampling procedure here, the system calculates the total sample size from the lot size. Select a sampling procedure that uses a valuation mode without valuation parameters.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the case of an inspection without a routing, master rec- ipe, or material specification, you have the following options to determine the inspection scope for a specific material:  100% inspection  Specify a percentage  Specify a sampling procedure without valuation parameters Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 64 100% Inspection There are two possible business scenarios that you need to consider while setting up this indicator:  Inspect without routing, master recipe, or material specification The system creates the sample size as equal to the cre- ated lot.  Inspect with routing, master recipe, or material speci- fication The sample size of the created lot is the same as the lot size. The sampling procedure set down in the inspection plan or specification isn’t taken into account in the sample determination process for the inspection characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Instead, the system uses sample determination rules, which are preset in the configuration. The sample size of the created charac- teristics depends on whether the base unit of measure has decimal places. If the base unit of measure does have decimal places, the sample size of the character- istic is always 1; if the base unit of measure doesn’t have decimal places, 100% of the lot size should be inspected in sample units of measure (rounded up) for the characteristic. Here, the dependencies are that if in addition to either 100% inspection , Inspect with Task List , or Insp. by Config- uration indicators, you also set the Skips Allowed charac- teristic, nothing changes in the sample calculation.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, the system does check whether the characteris- tic is to be inspected or not. Inspection % This field is of significance only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing, master recipe, task list, or material specification. In this case, the system calculates the over- all sample size using this percentage value from the inspection lot size. Manual Sample Calc. Set this indicator if you want to manually trigger the sam- ple calculation for the inspection lot. Manual Sample Entry If this checkbox is selected, then you need to manually enter the sample size for the inspection of this inspection lot.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This characteristic is only taken into account in inspections that don’t use a routing, task list, or material specification. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 65 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Dyn. Mod. Rule This is for the dynamic modification rule. It contains defi- nitions of the inspection levels and the conditions that cause inspection levels to change. This field is significant only in an inspection that doesn’t use a routing or mate- rial specification. If you enter a dynamic modification rule here, a quality level for the material, plant, and inspection type is set, and when the quality level is created automat- ically, the system calculates the dynamic modification cri- teria for the inspection-lot origin.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If, in addition to the sample size, you control using a sampling procedure, the system checks whether the combination of dynamic modification rule and sampling procedure is permitted (permitted relationships). Refer to Chapter 3, which cov- ers the dynamic modification rule in detail. Skips Allowed If you set this indicator, then the system allows skipping results recording for inspection characteristics when it calculates the sample size of the lot. The characteristic takes effect in the inspection lot if it’s set in the QM inspection data of the material for the inspection type in question.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the characteristic isn’t set in the dynamic modification process, the system selects the next nonskip inspection level instead of a skip level. If all the characteristics to be inspected in an inspection lot have the Skip status, it results in a skip inspection lot. In the case of a skip lot, if both skips and automatic usage decision are allowed, inspection-lot processing is carried out without any user intervention. A time delay can be set for this in the configuration. This triggers unrestricted stock at the goods receipt stage because the lot quantity is immediately posted to unrestricted-use stock.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the QM control function in procurement (quality infor- mation record), you can make a setting that skips the goods receipt inspections. You can also specify for the material in the inspection data that an inspection is to be carried out only for the first goods receipt per order or production order. To prevent individual characteristics from being skipped, proceed as follows:  Assign characteristic weightings to the characteristics to prevent skips.  Assign sampling procedures to the characteristics that don’t permit stage changes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 66 Automatic UD If you set this indicator, the system can automatically make usage decisions for inspection lots. The inspection lots have to fulfill the following conditions:  All characteristics are completed.  No characteristic has been rejected.  No defects have been recorded, and no quality notifi- cation has been created. The lead time set in configuration must have expired. Inspection lots with the status Skip Lot can also be con- sidered here. If an automatic usage decision can’t be made, you’ll have to make it manually.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system records an automatic usage decision in the long text that accompanies the usage decision. Chapter 3 shows you how to make automatic usage deci- sions for skipped inspection lots. Avg. Insp. Duration Specifies the average duration, in days, of the inspection for every inspection type. If the start date of the inspec- tion is entered during inspection-lot creation, the system calculates the end date using the average inspection time entered in this field. Conversely, if the end date of the inspection is entered during inspection-lot creation, the system calculates the start date using the average inspec- tion time entered in this field.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Q-Score Procedure The coded ID of the procedure that the system uses to cal- culate the quality score. You can maintain one quality score procedure per inspection type in the material mas- ter record. The system transfers the information main- tained in this field to the inspection lot record on inspection lot creation. In the simplest procedure, the quality score is taken from the code for the usage decision. In another procedure, the quality score is calculated on the basis of the scrap share in the inspected characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Allowed Scrap Share Some quality score procedures require an allowed scrap share to calculate the quality score. In normal cases, the scrap share is set to be half the acceptable quality level (AQL) value. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 67 2.1 Quality Management View in Material Master Control Lot Creation This control applies to goods receipt for inspection lot ori- gins 01, 04, 05, and 08. You can make the following settings:  <Space>: One inspection lot per goods receipt docu- ment item. In other words, one inspection lot is cre- ated for each goods receipt document item.  X : One inspection lot per purchase order item or order item and batch. If you set this value, the system cre- ates an inspection lot only for the first goods receipt for each purchase order item or production order, or, if the material is managed in batches, only for the first goods receipt per purchase order item or production order and batch.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This setting is restricted to the inspec- tion lot origins For Purchase Order (Inspection Lot Ori- gin 01) and For Production Order (Inspection Lot Origin 04) .  1 : One inspection lot per material document, material, and batch. If you set this value, the system opens only one inspection lot per material and batch (in the case of batch management) for a material document (i.e., within a goods receipt transaction). This can occur if several purchase orders or several partial deliveries of the same material are processed within one goods receipt transaction.  2 : One inspection lot per material and batch.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you set this value, the system opens only one inspection lot per material and batch (in the case of batch manage- ment). This setting is useful only for materials that require batch management. In the case of X , 1 , and 2 , if the stock of the inspection lot that was created with the first goods receipt isn’t com- pletely discharged or its usage decision made when fur- ther partial deliveries are received, these goods receipt quantities are added to this stock. In the case of 1 and 2 , if Skip Lot is set, there is no direct change of the stock type from In Quality Inspection to Unrestricted Use .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Instead, a transfer posting takes place as part of an automatic usage decision with a time delay. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 68 Tips and Tricks When you’re maintaining the control indicator of the inspection data, we recommend that you use the predefined and default configuration settings for each inspection type. This is important because different entries for the same inspection type cause different materials to be used or cause difficulties with the inspection-lot generation process. If a special inspection lot control process is required on the material level for the same inspection type, this must be carefully documented in each individual case.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For more information, see Chapter 3, which covers the configuration details of main- taining default values for inspection types. Table 2.3 contains a selective list of inspection types of respective inspection origins that we cover in various chapters of this book. The last column is the number of the chapter in which you’ll find detailed configuration, master data setup, requirements, or business processes that use the specific inspection type. Individual QM order This characteristic specifies that you need to create an individual QM order with an account assignment when the system creates an inspection lot for this inspection type.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you set this characteristic, you’re specifying that an individual QM order should be opened for this combi- nation of material and inspection type. If the field for the QM order is filled and the characteristic for individual QM orders is set, this field is taken into account only if the system is unable to create an individ- ual QM order due to a missing account assignment in the inspection lot. A prerequisite for creating an individual QM order is that the inspection lot contains an allocation provision such as sales order, cost center, or plant.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM Order A number that uniquely identifies the QM order to which the costs are to be charged. The QM order specified in the material master record in the inspection data is used as a template for inspection-lot creation if an individual QM order hasn’t been created for the inspection lot. Control Indicator Effects Table 2.2 Inspection Types Setup (Cont.) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 70 Note In project discussions, requests are often made to create new inspection types to meet specific business needs, such as inspection types that reflect different strategies for incoming inspections for fundamentally different materials. Even if you configure new or extra inspection types, the problem still remains. This is because the inspection ori- gins to which you have to assign the inspection type are preconfigured and delivered. You therefore have no choice but to individually change the relevant control indicators under Inspection Data in the Quality management view of the material.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In such a case, the only configuration tasks are to customize the short name of the inspection type and the global control indicator for each existing inspection type. For this reason, we don’t recommend that you create new inspection types to meet this business need. Chapter 3 shows how you can configure a new inspection type and use it in business processes. 2.2 Master Record This section covers the important QM master record, as well as other logistics areas needed in the SAP S/4HANA system to run business processes. 2.2.1 Change Master Record To manage the different versions of a drawing that belongs to a material master record, an inspection plan, or an inspection method, for example, it may be a good idea to also assign a version to every material.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can link every version of the material master record with a change master record. A change master record brings far greater control 16 1601 9 Initial test (stability study) 15 16 1602 9 Manual inspection lot for stor- age conditions 15 17 17 9 EWM inspection 8 17 1701 9 EWM: goods receipt inspection for purchase order 8 89 89 3 Other inspection 3 89 8914 4 Inspection checklists 7 Inspection Origin Inspection Type Task List Usage Inspection Type Description Chapter Table 2.3 Inspection Types (Cont.) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 71 2.2 Master Record and visibility to changes made to the QM master record, such as an inspection method or an inspection plan. Note See Chapter 13, which contains an example of using a change number to manage changes to an inspection plan. 2.2.2 Business Partner Master Record The supplier master record contains all the necessary information about a supplier from the purchasing and accounting points of view. In addition, the buyer can set a lock under the Lock Data option for quality reasons. This lock contains the same list entries as those in the quality info record for delivery control on the material supplier level.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The details of the contact persons for purchasing and QM are stored in the part- ner data of the supplier master. The customer master record, on the other hand, contains all the necessary information about a customer from the point of view of sales and accounting. The buyer can also set a lock, if necessary, for quality reasons. This master record also contains partner data, such as the contact person in the customer’s company. It can be useful to maintain the details of a contact person responsible for quality matters. 2.2.3 Batch Master If the company maintains an externally procured material or an in-house material through batch management, the system creates a batch master record using Transac- tion MSC1N or menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Batch  Create .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the relevant configuration settings in place, the system can automatically assign a batch number, or a user can do so manually for goods movements or for pro- cess or production orders. If batch management is active for a material, the system requires a batch number during inspections and can also assign the inspection lot data to the batches. An important consideration for process industries is that it’s a requirement to separate various batches of a material according to their different properties. To this end, batches are divided into different classes, which are defined in advance in the batch characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If during the inspection a batch fulfills the specification of a batch char- acteristic , it’s assigned to the relevant batch class . If a material with the required prop- erties is subsequently used for further processing or for a sales order, the batch classification finds the appropriate material. You also need the batch master record for order processing in production planning for process industries (PP-PI). Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 72 Figure 2.3 shows the Basic Data 1 tab of batch 6 of material RM17, plant 1710, and storage location 0001. The system automatically fills in the date of manufacture, shelf-life expiration date/best-before date (SLED/BBD), and next inspection date while running relevant business processes. Figure 2.3 Batch Master Note See Chapter 9 on batch management, which also covers the master data requirements, as well as the business processes that either fill up or automatically update the various fields that you see in Figure 2.3. 2.2.4 Production Resources and Tools All the resources required for production, such as documents, operating supplies, test equipment, tools, equipment, and so on, are within the scope of production resources/ tools (PRTs).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You need to assign the PRTs to the operations and inspection characteris- tics of a task list. Depending on the PRT type, the master record can be a material, doc- ument, PRT master record, or equipment master record. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 73 2.5 Work Center Note See Chapter 7 on QM integration with PM (test equipment management), which also covers various types of PRTs. The chapter includes cross-elements from quality plan- ning, repairs and maintenance (calibration tests), and their master records (equipment). 2.3 Master Recipe or Routing In this task list type, the work-scheduling function records all elements in the task plan- ning area, and the QM function records all data for inspection planning. The produc- tion steps and capacities are linked to the work centers, and the required control functions for the production order are determined.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The elements of inspection plan- ning, inspection characteristics, sampling procedure, and so on are fully integrated into the master recipe or routing. 2.4 Reference Operation Set The reference operation set contains virtually all the objects and functions of the rout- ing. It’s used mainly as a task list template for variations of a production procedure or as a general template. The individual operations in the reference operation set are refer- enced for this purpose in the routing or in the inspection plan (a fixed reference; every change in the reference operation set affects the inspection plan and the routing).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note The reference operation set, routing, and inspection plan are the same in terms of their structure and essential functions. This makes navigating in the different task list types quite simple for the inspection planner, who has to maintain the quality-relevant data in all task list types. Chapter 5 on production processes also covers details of the master recipe, routing, and reference operation set master data. 2.5 Work Center A quality work center is the physical or virtual location in which a user performs related quality inspection activities.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A work center is always plant-specific. The work center is a master record that’s important mainly for PP and controlling. It’s likewise usually maintained by the Production Planning and Control department. Every work center is assigned to a cost center so that the accounting department can analyze quality costs. To this end, the system calculates the costs that arise from the work performed at the work center on the basis of the allocation records for the individual cost centers. docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 76 2.6 Inspection Method An inspection method offers the provision to maintain detailed instructions for con- ducting physical or chemical quality tests of a material. The quality inspector can refer to the relevant inspection method for information or instruction while conducting an actual test. An inspection method can have several versions, which you can use to dif- ferentiate among various validity periods. To create an inspection method, use Transaction QS31 or follow menu path SAP  Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Method  Create .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen that appears, enter Insp. Method (inspection method) “QMINSP10” and Plant “1710”. You don’t need to enter the inspection method number or a date because the system automatically assigns an internal number to the inspection method and proposes a current date for the creation of the inspection method. Notice that it’s also possible to create a new inspection method by referencing an existing one. To create a new inspection method with reference to an already created inspection method, enter the details of reference fields such as plant, inspection method, key date, and version, and the system automatically copies all the information from the refer- ence inspection method to the new one.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can then change or update the new inspection method accordingly, saving data entry efforts. Tips and Tricks The option to create QM master data using templates or the copy function is generally available, and you can use it to quickly maintain master data, saving time and effort, as well as reducing data entry errors. In Figure 2.7, set the Status to 2 Released ; this makes the inspection method available during subsequent QM activities in which you use the inspection method. If the status of the inspection method is set to Being Created , it isn’t available in further QM activities.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can enter a short text, and a good search term always helps in finding the relevant information when you’re searching in the system. An entry in the Authorization Group field controls authorization to create or make changes, or even display an inspection method. You may want to allow very few people access to make changes to an inspec- tion method because it’s critical, sensitive information. Inspector Qualific. (inspector qualification) is the minimum credential or experience a person must have to perform the tasks listed in an inspection method—for example, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) certified quality inspector or total quality management (TQM) accredited expert.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose Long Text to create the long text of the inspection method; the system provides the option to write details of the inspection steps and procedures in the inspection method. It provides a Microsoft Word editor, with all the options normally available in Microsoft Word. In addition, there’s no limit to the amount of information you can enter as long text.
